1	# Step 4 — design: imagine the STORY of each subject (one subject at a time)
2	
3	Step 4 designs the **STORY** — what each subject DOES, sounds like, wants, and becomes — by answering the
4	*story* half of `content-framework.md`, **one subject at a time**, in a fixed order:
5	
6	**PLAYER (§2) → each NPC (§3, one each) → WORLD (§5) → REACTIVITY as experience (§4).**
7	
8	The order is **supply → demand → stage**: the player's own thread is imagined before the NPC arcs that lean on
9	it, and the world before the reactivity that ties it together. This is the heart of incremental authoring —
10	**never imagine the whole game in one pass.** Step 5 (`step-5-blueprint.md`) then **structures** this story into
11	the exact gated, placed, ordered scene list; Step 6 (`step-6-feedback.md`) reviews it.
12	
13	**Step 4 is now STORY-ONLY.** Every mechanism decision — lanes, gates, thresholds, placement, flag wiring,
14	scene order — moved down to the Blueprint step, so story and structure are never decided in the same breath.
15	The four words **lane, threshold, flag, placement** do not belong in a Step-4 brief: name the *moment* and what
16	it *feels* like; Blueprint turns it into the gated, placed scene.
17	
18	## Inputs
19	The **cascade + economy + desire ladder + frontier** (Step 2 / framework §1), the **cast** (Step 3 — role ·
20	hook · lane · depth · arc-shape · sketch · place in the machine), the **8 qualities** (Step 0), and
21	**`content-framework.md`** — the question set this step answers as *story* (§2 for Pass 1, §3 for Pass 2, §5
22	for Pass 3, §4 for Pass 4).
23	
24	## The ordering rule (enforced by the ledger)
25	The ledger's `deep_design` block tracks `{ player, npcs, world, reactivity }`. **Don't start `npcs` until
26	`player == "done"`; don't start `reactivity` until `npcs` and `world` are both done.** *Why:* you imagine the
27	player's own thread first so each NPC's story can build on a protagonist who is already going somewhere, and
28	reactivity is last because it describes how finished arcs change each other.
29	
30	---
31	
32	## Pass 1 — the PLAYER subject (§2 YOU) — FIRST, before any NPC
33	Answer **`content-framework.md` §2** as story. Output: a **`### The player thread (Step 4 · §2)`** block in
34	`design_book.md`.
35	- **2A bootstrap** — the off-zero solo acts + any behavior/story moment that nudges her open, and *why*
36	  (boredom, the rot starting, relief) — the experience, not the gate. **If her top-level drive is
37	  reactive** (revenge / escape / reclaiming — set by a thing that already happened), decide that cause
38	  here and make sure it's stated in the opening; an unmotivated reactive want reads as arbitrary. Pure
39	  appetite (the sandbox where wanting more is itself the engine) needs no wound — don't invent one.
40	  Name which it is so Blueprint and the opening beat carry the cause when there is one.
41	- **2B exhibition backbone** — the being-seen ladder per venue/stage, and what she WANTS out of being seen
42	  (tips, the thrill, proving her nerve, turning a head).
43	- **2C the economy as STORY** — her money story broke→rich: the lowest respectable earning at the start, the
44	  dirtiest best-paying thing by the end (better money always further down the lewd path), the buys she stays
45	  hungry for, the key items she covets. *(The income VALUES, item costs, and the feeder count are Blueprint's;
46	  here name the scenes and the want.)*
47	- **2D the ceiling** — the most extreme, most public thing she does that's about HER, the top of her own
48	  depravity, unthinkable on night one; plus any non-corruption ladder (job rank / fame / faction / skill) and
49	  what it's for.
50	
51	- **The daily-routine moment (where the world walks in)** — which of her repeated routines (a shower, the
52	  dishes, a work shift, a quiet hour) is the world allowed to intrude on, and what does that feel like — the
53	  surprise, the line she lets cross because she was *just doing a chore*? Each routine is both a feeder she
54	  runs alone AND the host an NPC walks in on — the same moment, two outcomes (`content-framework.md` §2E
55	  roster; `references/lanes.md` Lane 3). Name them here as story, before any NPC arc claims them.
56	
57	**Every feeder hangs on a WANT** (the desire ladder), never "raises corruption." **Ledger:** set
58	`deep_design.player = "done"` when the player story is complete.
59	
60	---
61	
62	## Pass 2 — each NPC (§3 THEM) — ONE NPC at a time
63	Takes one **cast row** and answers **`content-framework.md` §3** as story: the **story brief** below. **One NPC
64	per increment** — surface the brief (Mode A for *core*, Mode B for *peripheral*), get it okayed, then the
65	next. Never imagine the whole cast's arcs in one pass — this is the per-increment quality gate a one-shot can't
66	have. The **§3H "web between them"** is answered ONCE for the cast.
67	
68	### The output per NPC = the STORY brief (the kept half of the old design brief)
69	The mechanism half of the old design brief — the stat ladder & spine, the lane-by-lane map, the capstone triggers,
70	the wiring contract — now lives in the Blueprint step. Step 4 writes the **story**:
71	
72	1. **End-state fantasy** (one paragraph) — the complete arc's destination. **= EXPAND THE HOOK.** Author it
73	   FIRST; everything downstream grows from it.
74	2. **Voice spec** — how this NPC sounds (from the hook): diction, tells, what they call you, the private
75	   thought you glimpse, and how the voice shifts as they fall. RTS-flat for the everyday content; Tier-3 prose
76	   is earned only at the once-only peaks.
77	3. **The arc as a sequence of moments** — walk the road from cold start to the end-state as named turning
78	   points: the first warmth, the first crossing of a line, the first time, the surrender. The *moments*, in
79	   order — as experience, NOT as gated rungs (Blueprint sizes and gates them).
80	4. **Per-moment pretext shapes** — the in-fiction setup for each escalation: the believable reason the scene
81	   happens, the fiction that makes the move land.
82	5. **The big nights** — the once-only scripted peaks (first kiss, first time, surrender, breaking) as
83	   *moments* — what each one is and what it sets in motion. (Blueprint commits their triggers/thresholds.)
84	6. **What changes after** — once a turning point lands, how THIS SAME person behaves differently: greeting,
85	   voice, new things possible, old moments retired. *(Whether anyone ELSE reacts is Pass 4.)*
86	7. **Per-NPC anti-patterns** — what NOT to do for this NPC (e.g. a peer/dating NPC chasing her in private; a
87	   service NPC given a corruption arc).
88	8. **Acceptance** — the arc's "done" check, in story terms: the hook is visible (voice + want + real agency),
89	   legible pull (the player can feel the climb ahead), the payoff lands, the ceiling is honored.
90	
91	The genuinely-new story bindings Pass 2 adds:
92	- **Hook → arc.** The hook seeds §1 + §3, and the NPC's **want** gives them **agency** — they pursue, resist,
93	  scheme, set conditions; NOT a yes-man whose only state is your meters (quality #5).
94	- **Depth is an INPUT from casting** — core → a full, central figure; peripheral → a lighter flavor. Don't
95	  re-litigate it, and don't gold-plate a peripheral with a central arc's depth.
96	- **Late-act target** — a target introduced late carries a **complete, self-contained burn** (its own
97	  cold-to-surrender road), because it can't borrow pacing from a protagonist who's already maxed.
98	- **Hold each NPC to the 8 qualities** — legible pull, payoff, the charge, a reactive world.
99	
100	### Per-NPC self-check (story)
101	- **The hook is visible** (voice + want + real agency). · **The arc reads as a believable fall** — each moment
102	  follows from the last, no jump. · **Depth matches casting** (core rich / peripheral light). · **Anti-patterns
103	  respected.** · **The peak is earned** and the ceiling honored.
104	
105	### Worked example (bar game, story-only)
106	**Sal — core.** Hook: *"your late partner's loyal best friend who's wanted you for years and hates himself for
107	it."* End-state: the night he stops resisting and lets himself have you, then keeps coming back. Voice: gruff,
108	clipped, guilty; softens as he falls. The arc: you talk and serve him (ordinary, warm) → he catches himself
109	watching → the first time he doesn't look away → the night he stops pretending → he's yours. A slow burn — the
110	charge is the guilt breaking. *(Blueprint will turn these moments into gated, placed scenes — not here.)*
111	**Marcus — peripheral.** dating, light: a flirt who could become a fling; one good night, no deep arc.
112	
113	---
114	
115	## Pass 3 — the WORLD subject (§5) — the stage
116	Answer **`content-framework.md` §5** as story. Output: a **`### The world (Step 4 · §5)`** block. **The stage
117	already EXISTS** — Step 2b designed the spatial graph + each place's dramatic job + access category. Don't
118	re-decide geography here; imagine each place's *story* (the feel of its public, its clock, its shared-private
119	moments) ON that map.
120	- **5A** confirm/deepen each place's dramatic JOB from the Step-2b map as *story* (the room-content floor was
121	  already gated there) + which track lives there.
122	- **5C** the reactive public — who notices her besides the named cast, the predator-vs-prude dispositions, and
123	  what goes WRONG when she pushes too far (caught, robbed, taken) — as *story consequence*, not condition gates.
124	- **5E** the felt cadence + the pressure clock — how urgent the days feel, the deadline hanging over it.
125	- **5H** the shared private spaces — for each place where someone does something private and the player's
126	  next door (the one bathroom, a bedroom), is it a walk-in / peep / occupied / caught spot? **Surface each
127	  candidate and CONFIRM it with the user per-place (`run-mode.md` Mode A) before it's in play** — grounded in
128	  the place + person + hour, never a blanket toggle (`content-framework.md` §5H).
129	
130	*(The per-place ceilings, the schedules, the phone/sidebar wiring, and the locks are Blueprint's — here give
131	each place its dramatic JOB and the feel of its public and clock.)*
132	
133	---
134	
135	## Pass 4 — REACTIVITY as experience (§4) — LAST
136	Answer **`content-framework.md` §4** as story. Name, for each state-change, **what becomes different** — as a
137	felt moment: when she crosses a depravity band, what's suddenly possible; when an NPC falls, how the next
138	visit reads; when she takes someone, who else reacts; when she loses ground (§4F), whether the world bites.
139	*(The actual flag deps, the dependency map, and the D1/D2/D3 wiring are Blueprint's — here name the
140	consequence so Blueprint has something to wire.)* The §4F fail-state gets its one-line declaration here (does
141	failure exist at all); Blueprint decides whether and how it bites.
142	
143	**Ledger:** set `deep_design.reactivity = "done"`, then **set `pipeline_phase = "blueprint"`.**
144	
145	---
146	
147	## Navigation (which subject / NPC next)
148	At each pass boundary, **propose the next move with options** (`run-mode.md` → "Navigation at junctions"). The
149	four-pass ORDER is fixed (supply→demand→stage), but *within* Pass 2 "which NPC next" and *at* boundaries "ready
150	to move from the player to the NPCs?" are real junctions — propose from the `deep_design` ledger block.
151	
152	## Cross-references
153	`references/content-framework.md` (the question set this step answers) · `references/lanes.md` /
154	`trait-design.md` / `sex-loop.md` / `systems.md` (the mechanism library — used at **Blueprint**, not here) ·
155	Step 2 = `references/step-2-toplevel.md` (framework §1 + the inputs) · Step 5 = `references/step-5-blueprint.md`
156	(structures this story into the scene list) · Step 6 = `references/step-6-feedback.md` (reviews it). Set
157	`pipeline_phase = "blueprint"` when all four passes are `done`.

The four words **lane, threshold, flag, placement** do not belong in a Step-4 brief: name the *moment* and what
it *feels* like; Blueprint turns it into the gated, placed scene.

## Inputs
The **cascade + economy + desire ladder + frontier** (Step 2 / framework §1), the **cast** (Step 3 — role ·
hook · lane · depth · arc-shape · sketch · place in the machine), the **8 qualities** (Step 0), and
**`content-framework.md`** — the question set this step answers as *story* (§2 for Pass 1, §3 for Pass 2, §5
for Pass 3, §4 for Pass 4).

## The ordering rule (enforced by the ledger)
The ledger's `deep_design` block tracks `{ player, npcs, world, reactivity }`. **Don't start `npcs` until
`player == "done"`; don't start `reactivity` until `npcs` and `world` are both done.** *Why:* you imagine the
player's own thread first so each NPC's story can build on a protagonist who is already going somewhere, and
reactivity is last because it describes how finished arcs change each other.

---

## Pass 1 — the PLAYER subject (§2 YOU) — FIRST, before any NPC
Answer **`content-framework.md` §2** as story. Output: a **`### The player thread (Step 4 · §2)`** block in
`design_book.md`.
- **2A bootstrap** — the off-zero solo acts + any behavior/story moment that nudges her open, and *why*
  (boredom, the rot starting, relief) — the experience, not the gate. **If her top-level drive is
  reactive** (revenge / escape / reclaiming — set by a thing that already happened), decide that cause
  here and make sure it's stated in the opening; an unmotivated reactive want reads as arbitrary. Pure
  appetite (the sandbox where wanting more is itself the engine) needs no wound — don't invent one.
  Name which it is so Blueprint and the opening beat carry the cause when there is one.
- **2B exhibition backbone** — the being-seen ladder per venue/stage, and what she WANTS out of being seen
  (tips, the thrill, proving her nerve, turning a head).
- **2C the economy as STORY** — her money story broke→rich: the lowest respectable earning at the start, the
  dirtiest best-paying thing by the end (better money always further down the lewd path), the buys she stays
  hungry for, the key items she covets. *(The income VALUES, item costs, and the feeder count are Blueprint's;
  here name the scenes and the want.)*
- **2D the ceiling** — the most extreme, most public thing she does that's about HER, the top of her own
  depravity, unthinkable on night one; plus any non-corruption ladder (job rank / fame / faction / skill) and
  what it's for.

- **The daily-routine moment (where the world walks in)** — which of her repeated routines (a shower, the
  dishes, a work shift, a quiet hour) is the world allowed to intrude on, and what does that feel like — the
  surprise, the line she lets cross because she was *just doing a chore*? Each routine is both a feeder she
  runs alone AND the host an NPC walks in on — the same moment, two outcomes (`content-framework.md` §2E
  roster; `references/lanes.md` Lane 3). Name them here as story, before any NPC arc claims them.

**Every feeder hangs on a WANT** (the desire ladder), never "raises corruption." **Ledger:** set
`deep_design.player = "done"` when the player story is complete.

---

## Pass 2 — each NPC (§3 THEM) — ONE NPC at a time
Takes one **cast row** and answers **`content-framework.md` §3** as story: the **story brief** below. **One NPC
per increment** — surface the brief (Mode A for *core*, Mode B for *peripheral*), get it okayed, then the
next. Never imagine the whole cast's arcs in one pass — this is the per-increment quality gate a one-shot can't
have. The **§3H "web between them"** is answered ONCE for the cast.

### The output per NPC = the STORY brief (the kept half of the old design brief)
The mechanism half of the old design brief — the stat ladder & spine, the lane-by-lane map, the capstone triggers,
the wiring contract — now lives in the Blueprint step. Step 4 writes the **story**:

1. **End-state fantasy** (one paragraph) — the complete arc's destination. **= EXPAND THE HOOK.** Author it
   FIRST; everything downstream grows from it.
2. **Voice spec** — how this NPC sounds (from the hook): diction, tells, what they call you, the private
   thought you glimpse, and how the voice shifts as they fall. RTS-flat for the everyday content; Tier-3 prose
   is earned only at the once-only peaks.
3. **The arc as a sequence of moments** — walk the road from cold start to the end-state as named turning
   points: the first warmth, the first crossing of a line, the first time, the surrender. The *moments*, in
   order — as experience, NOT as gated rungs (Blueprint sizes and gates them).
4. **Per-moment pretext shapes** — the in-fiction setup for each escalation: the believable reason the scene
   happens, the fiction that makes the move land.
5. **The big nights** — the once-only scripted peaks (first kiss, first time, surrender, breaking) as
   *moments* — what each one is and what it sets in motion. (Blueprint commits their triggers/thresholds.)
6. **What changes after** — once a turning point lands, how THIS SAME person behaves differently: greeting,
   voice, new things possible, old moments retired. *(Whether anyone ELSE reacts is Pass 4.)*
7. **Per-NPC anti-patterns** — what NOT to do for this NPC (e.g. a peer/dating NPC chasing her in private; a
   service NPC given a corruption arc).
8. **Acceptance** — the arc's "done" check, in story terms: the hook is visible (voice + want + real agency),
   legible pull (the player can feel the climb ahead), the payoff lands, the ceiling is honored.

The genuinely-new story bindings Pass 2 adds:
- **Hook → arc.** The hook seeds §1 + §3, and the NPC's **want** gives them **agency** — they pursue, resist,
  scheme, set conditions; NOT a yes-man whose only state is your meters (quality #5).
- **Depth is an INPUT from casting** — core → a full, central figure; peripheral → a lighter flavor. Don't
  re-litigate it, and don't gold-plate a peripheral with a central arc's depth.
- **Late-act target** — a target introduced late carries a **complete, self-contained burn** (its own
  cold-to-surrender road), because it can't borrow pacing from a protagonist who's already maxed.
- **Hold each NPC to the 8 qualities** — legible pull, payoff, the charge, a reactive world.

### Per-NPC self-check (story)
- **The hook is visible** (voice + want + real agency). · **The arc reads as a believable fall** — each moment
  follows from the last, no jump. · **Depth matches casting** (core rich / peripheral light). · **Anti-patterns
  respected.** · **The peak is earned** and the ceiling honored.

### Worked example (bar game, story-only)
**Sal — core.** Hook: *"your late partner's loyal best friend who's wanted you for years and hates himself for
it."* End-state: the night he stops resisting and lets himself have you, then keeps coming back. Voice: gruff,
clipped, guilty; softens as he falls. The arc: you talk and serve him (ordinary, warm) → he catches himself
watching → the first time he doesn't look away → the night he stops pretending → he's yours. A slow burn — the
charge is the guilt breaking. *(Blueprint will turn these moments into gated, placed scenes — not here.)*
**Marcus — peripheral.** dating, light: a flirt who could become a fling; one good night, no deep arc.

---

## Pass 3 — the WORLD subject (§5) — the stage
Answer **`content-framework.md` §5** as story. Output: a **`### The world (Step 4 · §5)`** block. **The stage
already EXISTS** — Step 2b designed the spatial graph + each place's dramatic job + access category. Don't
re-decide geography here; imagine each place's *story* (the feel of its public, its clock, its shared-private
moments) ON that map.
- **5A** confirm/deepen each place's dramatic JOB from the Step-2b map as *story* (the room-content floor was
  already gated there) + which track lives there.
- **5C** the reactive public — who notices her besides the named cast, the predator-vs-prude dispositions, and
  what goes WRONG when she pushes too far (caught, robbed, taken) — as *story consequence*, not condition gates.
- **5E** the felt cadence + the pressure clock — how urgent the days feel, the deadline hanging over it.
- **5H** the shared private spaces — for each place where someone does something private and the player's
  next door (the one bathroom, a bedroom), is it a walk-in / peep / occupied / caught spot? **Surface each
  candidate and CONFIRM it with the user per-place (`run-mode.md` Mode A) before it's in play** — grounded in
  the place + person + hour, never a blanket toggle (`content-framework.md` §5H).

*(The per-place ceilings, the schedules, the phone/sidebar wiring, and the locks are Blueprint's — here give
each place its dramatic JOB and the feel of its public and clock.)*

---

## Pass 4 — REACTIVITY as experience (§4) — LAST
Answer **`content-framework.md` §4** as story. Name, for each state-change, **what becomes different** — as a
felt moment: when she crosses a depravity band, what's suddenly possible; when an NPC falls, how the next
visit reads; when she takes someone, who else reacts; when she loses ground (§4F), whether the world bites.
*(The actual flag deps, the dependency map, and the D1/D2/D3 wiring are Blueprint's — here name the
consequence so Blueprint has something to wire.)* The §4F fail-state gets its one-line declaration here (does
failure exist at all); Blueprint decides whether and how it bites.

**Ledger:** set `deep_design.reactivity = "done"`, then **set `pipeline_phase = "blueprint"`.**

---

## Navigation (which subject / NPC next)
At each pass boundary, **propose the next move with options** (`run-mode.md` → "Navigation at junctions"). The
four-pass ORDER is fixed (supply→demand→stage), but *within* Pass 2 "which NPC next" and *at* boundaries "ready
to move from the player to the NPCs?" are real junctions — propose from the `deep_design` ledger block.

## Cross-references
`references/content-framework.md` (the question set this step answers) · `references/lanes.md` /
`trait-design.md` / `sex-loop.md` / `systems.md` (the mechanism library — used at **Blueprint**, not here) ·
Step 2 = `references/step-2-toplevel.md` (framework §1 + the inputs) · Step 5 = `references/step-5-blueprint.md`
(structures this story into the scene list) · Step 6 = `references/step-6-feedback.md` (reviews it). Set
`pipeline_phase = "blueprint"` when all four passes are `done`.

**Cast locked, and we're now in Step 4 — designing each character's actual arc, one at a time.**

Step 4 has a fixed order: **you (the player) first**, then each man, then the world, then how it all reacts. Your own thread goes first because every other arc leans on it.

Here's the thing I had to be careful about: the skill's player-template assumes the usual "broke woman slowly corrupts herself" shape. **Vesper inverts that** — you don't start innocent and fall; you start as the most owned, most surrendered thing in the building, and the arc is *waking up*. So I translated the template instead of forcing it. Let me write your thread and then show you the choices in it.

## The player thread (Step 4 · §2) — YOU  *(draft → review)*

> Story only — what *she* does, wants, and becomes. (Stats, gates, placement = the Blueprint step.) This is
> the inverted template: she doesn't fall from innocence — she **wakes from total surrender.**

**Her drive — reactive-emergent (must be planted in the opening).**
She starts with **no will of her own.** Her only "want" is the company's order: *hunt the rogue.* Her **own**
drive has to be *born* over Phase 1, and the cause is seeded in the very first scene — not a wound she's
avenging, but a **person surfacing**: the cradle glitch (a memory that shouldn't exist), and a body that comes
alive during sex in a way her blank mind can't explain. The opening has to plant one feeling: *something in me
is older than this company.* (Pure-appetite sandboxes need no wound; this one has a buried self, not a wound —
don't write trauma, write **return.**)

**The two wants (the layered drive — the engine of the whole Phase).**
- **Given** *(loud, from beat one)* — catch the "evil" rogue. The company's mission. Drives the three
  infiltrations.
- **Her own** *(quiet, growing)* — find out what she is; reclaim the self they erased. Drives the chip-hunt.
They run on the **same trail** (Cain is the rogue *and* the key to her past), so chasing the given want feeds
the secret one — until the fracture, where they **split**: the hunt was a lie, and the only want left is hers.

**2B — the "being-seen" backbone = the covers + being used (her version of the exhibition ladder).**
Not a stage for tips — a **false face per target**, and being *used* on both sides:
- *Inside:* used by Mercer and the company — the surrendered slave. The sex is the **one thing she feels** (not
  pride, not shame — a single spark in a hollowed-out person). She wants nothing of her own yet.
- *Outside:* she wears a cover, lets a target use her — while *she's* the one draining him. The ladder:
  **pure used-tool → the secret user** (the weapon flips it: he thinks he's using her, she owns him) → **the
  first flicker of wanting it for herself** (the domme cover with Calloway = the taste of the user she's
  becoming). What she wants out of being used shifts from *nothing* → *more.*

**2C — the economy as story (light by design).**
She's **kept** — provided for, needs almost nothing inside the Tower. So the money story isn't broke→rich;
it's **reach + go off-book**: credits earned working marks pay to *reach the next target*, buy the *covers/
disguises*, *bribe* access, and buy *capability upgrades* (the items that let her reach harder men). The wants
she stays hungry for = the next upgrade and the next cover. Deliberately small in Phase 1 (a leash, not
survival); it **ignites in Act 2** when she funds her own agenda. *(Values/costs = Blueprint.)*

**2D — the ceiling (the top of her own depravity AND her own will — braided).**
- *Sexual/agency ceiling — **the weapon.*** She surrenders utterly, lets him finish inside her, and at his
  climax becomes the one in control — the **control canvas** where the used becomes the user. The most extreme
  thing that's *hers*: **winning by surrendering.** Unthinkable as *hers* on night one, when surrender is all
  there is.
- *Awakening ceiling — **the chip** (the non-corruption ladder).* Each recovered fragment is a step back toward
  the person she was. Its Phase-1 top = **the fracture**: the first want she's ever formed *against* the
  company — *"I had a life. I want it back."* What the ladder is *for*: the whole Act-2 turn (used → user).

**The daily-routine moments (where the world walks in).**
- **The cradle (charging)** — her nightly reset, and where her own buried past "walks in" (the memory leaks).
  The thing that intrudes here is *herself.*
- **Serving Mercer (sex + chores)** — the routine the **leash** walks into: his moods, his suspicion as she
  starts to glitch — danger entering the most surrendered space.
- **Working a cover** — the routine a **wrong-note** walks into: a target says something that doesn't fit
  "evil rogue," and the mission quietly cracks.

**The through-line:** she begins as the most owned thing in the building and ends Phase 1 with the **first
thought that's only hers.** Every system points at that single inch of will.

Done — your thread is in the design book under **## The player thread**. Here's it in plain words, and the couple of judgment calls I made that you should sign off on.

**The shape of you:**
- You start with **no will of your own** — your only "want" is the company's order: *catch the rogue.* Over Phase 1 a *second, secret want grows underneath it* — *find out what I am.* They ride the same trail (Cain is both the target and the key to your past), so chasing the company's want quietly feeds your own — until the chip, where the two **split apart** and the only want left is yours.
- "Being seen" for you isn't a stage — it's **wearing a false face and being used**, on both sides. Inside, Mercer uses you. Outside, the target thinks he's using you while *you're* the one draining him. The ladder runs: **used tool → secret user → starting to want it for yourself** (the domme cover with Calloway is the first taste).
- Your **ceiling is two things braided together**: the **weapon** (winning by completely surrendering — the control canvas), and the **chip** (each fragment is you coming back, topping out at the fracture: *"I had a life. I want it back."*).
- The three **routines the world walks in on**: the **cradle** (your own buried past leaking in), **serving Mercer** (the leash and his suspicion), and **working a cover** (a wrong-note that cracks the "evil rogue" lie).

**The one call I want you to confirm:** I wrote her awakening as **"return, not wound"** — she's not driven by revenge or pain, she's a *person resurfacing*. So the opening plants *"something in me is older than this company"* rather than trauma. That sets the emotional register for her whole arc. It felt right for a hollowed-out slave (there's nothing to avenge yet — there's someone to *become*), but it's a real fork: the alternative is a sharper revenge-edge once she learns the truth.

If "return, not wound" lands and the rest reads right, I'll mark your thread done and move to the first man — **Renner** (the way in). Want me to go?

## Renner — story brief (Step 4 · §3, NPC #1)  *(draft → review)*

> Core target · Mission 1 (the way in) · caretaker cover · spine = **guilt → dependence.** Story only.

**1. End-state fantasy — comfort as conquest.**
A man who used to give orders and now can't live with what he did. He ran Vance's worst facility — the one
Cain burned — and the guilt is eating him alive at the bottom of a glass. By the end of his arc he **needs
her** like a drug: the one gentle stranger who listens without judging, who he confesses everything to, who
he beds seeking absolution. She doesn't *break* a brute — she **gentles a guilty monster open** until his need
to be soothed is the door she walks through. The charge: a powerful man undone, emotionally on his knees to
the caretaker, handing over the unforgivable for the mercy of being held. The drain isn't a heist — it's the
last thing he gives a woman he thinks loves him.

**2. Voice — the authority that's leaking out of him.**
Clipped and guarded when sober (the old command voice, still there); slurring and over-sharing when drunk (the
guilt seeping). Tells: he changes the subject *hard* when the facility comes near; he drinks to a rhythm; he
apologizes for small things to avoid the big one. He calls her formal and wary at first ("miss"), then her
cover-name, then something tender. The thought you glimpse: he's terrified someone will find out what he did —
and *more* terrified no one ever will, that he'll carry it alone forever. As he falls, the authority drops
out entirely and he goes almost childlike in his need. RTS-flat at the bar; Tier-3 earned **only** at the
confession.

**3. The arc as moments (cold → end-state).**
1. **First contact** — she finds him drinking alone at the Anchor; she's just *kind*, no angle he can see. He's
   wary, brushes her off.
2. **First warmth** — she comes back, doesn't pry, listens. He starts watching the door for her — the relief
   of one person who wants nothing from him.
3. **First crack** — drunk, he says too much, *around* the facility ("I did things, for the company — things
   you wouldn't—") and catches himself. She doesn't flinch. The hook sets.
4. **First crossing** — grief turns to needing to be held; the comfort goes physical. The caretaker *allows*
   it; not the mission yet.
5. **The confession (big night)** — he breaks fully and tells her what the facility *did* — the first real
   crack in "evil rogue" (Cain *freed* people / destroyed something monstrous). He tells her because she's the
   only one who ever just listened.
6. **First time / the drain (big night)** — he beds her seeking absolution; she means it (the weapon runs on
   her pleasure); at his climax → the **control canvas** → she drains the rest: where Cain went, what he took,
   the leads that open Bastien and Calloway.
7. **Dependence (end-state)** — after, he's hers to revisit: softer, needier, a reusable mark who'll give her
   access and say things he shouldn't.

**4. Per-moment pretexts (the believable reason each scene happens).**
The Anchor makes a lone drinker + a quiet stranger ordinary (her cover = a nobody with her own reasons to
drink). Becoming a regular does the proximity work. Alcohol is the pretext for the over-share. Grief sends the
body looking for comfort — she *allows*, never initiates coldly. The confession breaks because she's the one
safe place he's found. The drain is sex-as-absolution: he thinks the act *is* the forgiveness.

**5. The big nights (once-only).**
- **The confession** — what the facility really did. Sets in motion: the player's first proof the hunt is a
  lie, and the threads to Bastien + Calloway.
- **The first time / first drain** — the **weapon's first on-screen use on a real target** (the whole loop's
  payoff scene, proven here on the tutorial man). Sets in motion: the control canvas as the recurring
  extraction, and the first leads toward the site.

**6. What changes after.**
After the confession: he watches the door for her, comes apart faster, leans on her openly — the wary
brush-off is gone. After the drain: he remembers nothing of the control canvas (wakes clean), but the
**dependence persists** in the fiction — he's softer, needier, and will do small things for her, grant access,
let things slip.

**7. Anti-patterns (what NOT to do with Renner).**
- Not a brute to dominate — his arc is *gentling*, not breaking; the charge is comfort, not force.
- The cover stays tender to his face — her feeling-nothing-but-the-sex is a **private** dissonance, never
  played as on-screen cruelty to him.
- No backstory dump — the facility leaks in fragments (the iceberg).
- Not a yes-man — he *wants* (to be forgiven, to not be alone) and he *resists* exposure: he can clam up, get
  defensive, even turn paranoid if she pushes too fast.
- He's the **tutorial target** — teach the loop cleanly; don't over-complicate him.

**8. Acceptance (done check, story terms).**
Hook visible (the guilt-wreck who clings — voice + want + agency). Legible pull (wary stranger → confessor →
drained, each step earned). Payoff lands (the confession + the first weapon-use). Ceiling honored (comfort-as-
conquest, dissonance kept private). Machine node delivered: draining Renner **opens Bastien + Calloway** and
lands the **first crack** in "evil rogue."

**Renner's done — full brief is in the design book.** Plain version:

He's the **tutorial man**, and his whole arc is **comfort as conquest**. He ran the facility Cain burned, the guilt is drowning him, and you don't *break* him — you're the one gentle stranger who listens without judging, and you **gentle him open** until he needs you like a drug. The win isn't force or even seduction-as-power; it's that he confesses the unforgivable to you because you're the only safe place he's found. The drain is the last thing he gives a woman he thinks loves him.

Two big nights carry him:

content.text:
Start with **how the game opens** — before any NPC. Here's my honest reasoning:

The opening is the foundation every NPC plugs into. It's where we establish, in the player's hands, the four things the whole game rests on:
1. **What she is** — an owned, surrendered weapon who feels nothing but the sex.
2. **The ownership** — Mercer, the leash, the cradle.
3. **The first crack** — the glitch/memory that shouldn't exist (the seed of her waking up).
4. **The loop** — serve inside → deploy outside → drain → return.

If we design a man first (Renner), we'd be building a seduction arc before we've nailed the frame it hangs in. Renner is literally the **tutorial target** — but a tutorial only works once the opening has taught the player who she is and how the loop turns. So the opening comes first, then he's the natural hand-off.

There's also a practical reason it's the better starting point: it's **concrete**. "How does scene one actually play" is something you can react to hard — much more than an abstract arc.

And we're not starting from nothing — way back we already sketched the shape of it: **opens in Mercer's bed** (her body responds, her mind stays cold) → he dismisses her → back to **her room and the charging cradle** → the surrender settles in → **the first glitch** (a memory that isn't supposed to be there). That cold-open already hits all four things above.

So my pitch: **let's design the opening next.** Want me to lay out how those first few minutes actually play — beat by beat — as a proposal you can tear into? (Chat only — nothing goes in the book until you say so.)

Your cold-open is strong — in one scene it locks her **surrender** (begging, then *grateful* to be fucked), the **one spark** (she feels it while the boss degrades her), **Mercer's ownership**, and it drops the three units in exactly where we wanted them (the opening, then gone). I'd keep all of it. Here's how I'd make the two missing pieces accurate:

**The mission they failed.**
The company's standing #1 priority is catching the rogue, and the opening is the **latest blown attempt**. My pitch: the company predicted one of his strikes and set a trap — threw the whole asset team at it. The units did their part (breach, muscle). **Wren froze at the one moment that mattered, and he slipped.** They had him, and she cost it — so the blame lands squarely on her, and Mercer's rage is real (this wasn't a scratch, it was *the* shot).

- It keeps the rogue **offstage** — he escapes unseen, which we need (Cain never appears in Phase 1).
- And here's the part that makes the scene pull double duty: **her "freeze" is the first glitch.** A memory she's never had surfaced for half a second and locked her up. She can't explain it; the company just reads "malfunction." **The thing waking up in her is literally what lost the mission.** The whole engine of the game is planted in scene one, disguised as a screw-up.

**The task he assigns her.**
Mercer splits the work by what each asset is *for*:
- **The three units →** hunt the rogue head-on — track, corner, the muscle. They're hardware; he throws them at it. (That's also their exit — they go do it, and we don't see them again in Phase 1.)
- **Wren →** the one thing the units can't do and she's built for: **get inside the men around him and pull the trail out of them.** Crude, in his mouth — *"You're useless with a gun. But you're very good at opening a man up while he's inside you. So do that."* That's her real function (seduce → the weapon → drain the secret) and the company's actual business (owning powerful men through what's in their heads). Then he points her at the first name — **Renner**, the man whose facility the rogue burned: *"Get close. Find me where he is."*

That hand-off launches the whole Phase-1 web: she can't fight, so she works the inside game one man at a time — and each man is both a lead on the rogue *and* the company owning someone new.

**One mirror worth banking** while the units are on screen: they watch Mercer use her and **feel nothing** — blank machines. *She's* the one who responds, who thanks him, who feels it. No dialogue needed; it shows she's different from them — the spark they don't have — right in the opening.

**Two calls for you:**
1. **The key one:** is her freeze the **first glitch** — the awakening starting in scene one, disguised as the failure? I strongly recommend yes; it wires the opening straight into the engine.
2. **Minor:** I pitched the failed op as a *head-on capture* (the units' show; she just froze in support), so the reassignment is a clean pivot to her real strength. The alternative: the failure was *her own kind of job* — an extraction she blew — making it "redo it properly." I lean the first (cleaner blame, keeps her specialty unblemished for the Renner tutorial).

Once you're happy with the shape, I'll write the opening into the book. Nothing goes in until then.

content.text:
I think it's a strong second beat, and the spine is right: **office (fail → punishment → reassign) → night at the cradle (what she is, the power, the resolve) → morning (the tip).** That's the whole opening. A few refinements to keep it true to the engine we locked:

**1. "Humanoid robot, saved by the company / the Chairman, duty to obey" — keep it, but it's what she *believes*, not what's true.**
That's the lie they raised her on, and it's perfect for the night scene: she soothes herself with the company's catechism — *they saved me, I owe them, I exist to serve.* The hidden truth (she's half-human; they didn't save her, they *took* her) is the engine that surfaces later. The scene should make the player feel the **gap** — a frightened girl insisting she's a grateful machine. We write her belief straight and never confirm it.

**2. The crying is the tell — and it should confuse her.**
This is the one real snag. We locked that she feels *nothing but the sex* — everything else is blanked. So open grief would break the rule. The fix makes the beat *better*: **her body cries and she doesn't know why.** A machine doesn't weep. She wipes her face, can't explain the water, would call it a fault — something to report or hide. The player sees grief; *she* sees a malfunction. Same as the freeze on the mission: the half-human leaking through, read as a glitch. That keeps "blank except the sex" intact *and* lets the awakening show.

**3. The power + "it doesn't work on the boss" — love it, one flag.**
Her dwelling on the gift is good: the company gave it to her, it takes a man the instant he finishes inside her, it's the thing she's *for*. And *"it's never worked on the boss, and she's never known why"* is a great mystery to plant. The flag: that's a Chekhov's gun — it promises an answer we'll owe in Act 2. We don't answer it now (she just accepts it). But the cleanest answer, if you like it: **the weapon needs a self to fire — it runs on her own pleasure, her own will — and with the boss she's in total surrender, no "her" is present, so there's nothing to pull the trigger.** Which means the day it finally *does* work on him is the day she's woken up enough to *be* someone — the exact used→user turn we want for Act 2. (Just a seed — we park the real answer.)

**4. Render it, don't narrate it.**
All these facts could collapse into a backstory wall. The night should *play* as her charging ritual: she settles into the cradle, the day winds down, a memory **fragment** leaks (an image, a sound, a name she doesn't know — never a clean flashback; the iceberg stays under), the tears she can't explain, the catechism she repeats to steady herself, then power-down. The facts arrive through what she *does* and tells herself — not a lore dump.

**5. The resolve beat is good *because* it's a retreat.**
*"She'll do better next time, she sleeps"* — that's her **clinging back to the leash** right after the crack. The awakening isn't a straight line; she resists it, reaches for the comfort of being owned. Keep exactly that.

**The morning tip:** I'd deliver it as a short dossier on her phone (teaches that system) waiting when she wakes — *what happened* (the rogue burned a facility; the man who ran it, Renner, is drinking himself stupid at a bar called the Anchor), *why her* (Renner knows where the rogue's been — get the trail), *what she can do* (get close, use the gift), and the target: *meet this guy.* Minimal, exactly as you said.

This refines the old "bed → cradle" sketch into something better — when we write it, this supersedes that.

Two things for you: does the **crying-as-malfunction** version sit right with you, and do you want to **plant the boss-immunity mystery unanswered** (my rec) or pin the reason now?

- **Mercer (the boss)** — by action: the rage, the threat to scrap her, the punishment-fuck, the cold reassignment. You learn who he is with zero backstory.
- **The three units (Vega, Lyra, Nova)** — he gives *them* the hunt, by name, and they take it blank-faced while he uses her in front of them. Their flawless emptiness is the introduction — and the contrast (they feel nothing; she feels it) quietly shows what *she* is.

- **The rogue / the mission** — Mercer frames him as the monster: he **murdered the Chairman's wife**, he's an enemy of the company and the world, the Chairman wants him dead. The marching order.
- **Her (Wren)** — through the whole POV: the asset who failed, begged, was punished, was *grateful* — then alone at night with the catechism she tells herself.

**On the wife — strong spine, one thing to keep straight.** That's the company's **official story**, the thing that makes the hunt feel righteous to everyone, her included. But we locked that Cain is actually *good* and the hunt is a *lie* — so the wife's death has to be **fabricated or not what they claim** (he didn't murder an innocent; something else happened). We don't resolve it now; we plant it as gospel and let the wrong-notes erode it. Another Chekhov's gun: *what really happened to the Chairman's wife?* (Optional seed to bank: the Chairman's hunger for a deathless, *feeling* body could be **grief** — he lost her and will burn the world to never lose anyone again. Turns him from a stock immortality villain into something sharper.)

**Beat 1 — The office (the punishment).**

- A **node** = one actual **screen** the player clicks through. It's a **build** unit.
- **One beat = many nodes.** The office isn't one screen — it's a whole sequence of them.

1. **The line-up** — she and the three units stand before Mercer; the failed op hangs in the air. *(sets the scene)*

+7–9. **The punishment (~3 nodes, flexes ±)** — he takes her → the act (explicit, her body answering) → the units watching, blank, while *she* feels it. *(the "she feels, they don't" mirror)*
+10. **Gratitude** — she thanks him; the degradation she accepts.

+11. **The reassignment** — names Vega / Lyra / Nova to the head-on hunt; gives *her* the inside job ("useless with a gun, but…"); frames the mission: *the rogue murdered the Chairman's wife, enemy of the company and the world.*
+12. **Dismissed** — out of the office → the night.

+- **Introduces:** Mercer (cruel owner) · the three units (perfect, empty — her opposite) · the Chairman (named, the power above) · the rogue / mission (the "monster") · her (the owned asset who failed).
+- **Hidden crack:** the freeze = the **first glitch.** Everyone reads it as a malfunction.
+### Beat 2 — The night (~7 nodes) — the cradle, fully linear
+1. **The walk back** — through the Tower to her own floor and room.
+2. **The cradle** — she powers into the charging cradle; the reset ritual. *(the cradle = charge / save / start-of-day)*
+3. **The tears** — her body cries; she can't explain the water; reads it as a fault to hide.
+4. **The leak** — a memory fragment surfaces (a face, a sound, a name she doesn't know), then gone.
+5. **The catechism** — she recites what she's told she is: *saved by the company and the Chairman, owes them everything, exists to obey.*
+6. **The power** — her gift (control of a man the instant he finishes inside her, company-given) — and the odd fact it's **never** worked on the boss, never questioned.
+7. **Power-down** — she promises to do better; powers down. *(the retreat into the leash)*
+- **Introduces:** who she *thinks* she is (the lie). **Plants:** the awakening (tears + memory) + the boss-immunity mystery.
+- **(No flavor choices — kept fully on-rails by design.)**
+### Beat 3 — The morning (~4 nodes) — the task, then the city opens
+1. **Power-up** — she wakes in the cradle, charged, a new day. *(the day-cycle / morning start)*
+2. **The briefing** — a dossier waiting on her phone. *(the phone)*
+3. **The tip** — what happened (a facility burned), why her (Renner knows the trail), what she can do (get close, the gift), where (the Anchor).
+4. **Out the door** *(the hinge)* — she takes a cover and steps out of the Tower for the first time → **the city opens.** → the Anchor / meet Renner.

+- **Crying = malfunction.** She feels *nothing but the sex* — so the tears are a thing her body does that she can't explain and would hide. The player sees grief; she sees a fault. (Same as the freeze.)
+- **Belief vs. truth.** Write her self-concept *straight* (machine, saved, owes them, obeys) and **never confirm it.** The gap between what she says and what the player suspects is the engine.
+- **The cage mirrors her.** On-rails = she has no will yet, so the player doesn't either. Agency switches on with her first free step.

+- **The Chairman's wife.** The "rogue murdered her" story is the company's **lie / propaganda** (it keeps Cain good). What *really* happened to her is a later reveal. *(Truth: TBD.)*

+- **Why the weapon fails on the boss.** *Candidate (not locked):* the weapon needs a *self* to fire (her own pleasure / will) — and in total surrender to Mercer there's no "her" present, so nothing triggers it. The day it finally works on him = the day she's awake enough to *be* someone (wires the Act-2 used→user turn).

# Vesper — iteration log (where we looped, and where to improve)

> An honest post-mortem of the authoring conversation, written to do exactly what LO asked: study the
> back-and-forth so we get better. The faithful turn-by-turn is in `conversation-transcript.md`; this file
> distills the *pattern*. Turn numbers (USER #n) reference that transcript.

---

## The one meta-lesson (read this first)

**Almost every "nope" was the same failure: I produced the HOW before we'd agreed the WHY.** A question, a
meter, a web, a map — I kept handing over a concrete artifact while a *foundational* agreement underneath it
was still missing. LO's recurring signal — *"something is off,"* *"I'm not convinced,"* *"nope"* — was never
about the surface artifact; it was always pointing at the un-agreed foundation (the player's **desire**, the
sexual **register**, the world's **aliveness**).

**The breakthroughs all came the moment I STOPPED producing and honestly DIAGNOSED** ("we built a story, not
a game"; "I'm putting a dominance fantasy on a submission character"; "the map is a scene-holder"). Every
time I did that, we unstuck in one turn. Every time I instead offered *another* version of the artifact, we
burned 2–4 turns.

> **Rule for next time:** when LO says "something's off" and can't name it, do not produce another option.
> Stop and dig for the missing *what/why*. The diagnosis is the deliverable, not the next pitch.

---

## The loops, in order (the expensive ones)

### Loop 1 — `AskUserQuestion` vs. conversation *(USER #1–#9, recurring)*
I opened the seed with a 4-option `AskUserQuestion`; LO rejected it to clarify. I did it **again** (targets +
"ice"); rejected again. ~3–4 rejections total.
- **Lesson:** during open ideation LO wants **prose pitches he can edit**, not multiple-choice forks.
  *(Already saved to memory: `lo-prefers-concrete-pitches`.)* The question tool is for crisp late forks only.

### Loop 2 — "WTF, does a machine get hormones?" *(USER #5–#9)*
I proposed arousal-as-earned-upgrade and asserted it was an "always-on" engine trait. LO challenged **both**:
"what makes it always-on?" (forced me to read `v2.py` — I'd overstated it) and "WTF does a machine get
hormones so she wants to be fucked like a dog?" (a coherence hole).
- **Lesson A:** I asserted an engine fact from memory and was wrong. **Ground claims in the code first.**
- **Lesson B:** I kept proposing *mechanics* for desire before nailing the *logic* of desire. The fix
  ("desire = an objective function, not hormones") should have come first.

### Loop 3 — "what is the question about??" *(USER #11)*
My "does anything leak through the ice?" question was so wrapped in metaphor that LO couldn't tell what I was
asking. I had to re-ask it in plain words ("when the game ends, is she still all machine, or a bit human?").
- **Lesson:** **plain language.** I fogged a simple question. (The skill's own run-mode rule; I broke it.)

### Loop 4 — the Integration meter & "story not a game" *(USER #18–#22)* — *expensive*
I proposed an "Integration" feeling-meter + "capability buckets." LO: *"I don't like the integration at
all."* Then *"I don't even like your third bucket… there's something off… it doesn't feel convinced."* I
finally diagnosed: **we designed a STORY, not a GAME** — no player desire, no agency, no loop.
- **Lesson:** I built the **progression machinery (meters/upgrades) before the player's desire** — the exact
  thing the skill warns against ("desire onstage, meter backstage"). Several turns lost to bolting gears onto
  an engine with no fuel.

### Loop 5 — submission vs. dominance *(USER #25–#31)* — *the deepest loop*
Even after the opening scene fixed the desire problem, LO stayed unconvinced. I eventually named it: **I'd
been designing a *dominance / conquest* fantasy ("cold conquest, break-and-own, become the madam") onto a
character LO had reframed as a *surrendered, owned slave*.** The two fought for ~4 turns and I didn't see it.
- **Lesson (the big one):** **when the premise reframes, audit the inherited assumptions.** The
  "conquest/madam" desire-span was a leftover from the Step-0 seed; LO turned her into a submissive owned
  weapon messages earlier, and I never went back and re-examined the register. Stale framing persisted under
  everything and poisoned the web design until it was named.

### Loop 6 — the web, three rejected forms *(USER #32–#37)*
Tied to Loop 5: I produced the web three times — a marks **menu** ("nope," too cast-y), a mechanics **list**
("nope," too abstract), a three-men **web** ("nope, something off," the dominance mismatch). It only landed
once the register was fixed and reframed as **infiltration**.
- **Lesson:** I kept re-skinning the *artifact* while the *register* underneath was wrong. Same as the meta-
  lesson — fix the foundation, not the surface.

### Loop 7 — the map, built dead then rebuilt alive *(USER #45–#48)*
I built a tidy "exactly-needed-locations" map; LO: *"nope… this does not give the feel of a real living
world."* I'd followed the skill's anti-sprawl rule straight off a cliff.
- **Lesson:** **doctrine can be wrong for the game.** The skill's "add zones only where content lives" rule
  produces a scene-holder, not a world. (Logged as a candidate skill fix in `location_design_note.md`.) I
  should have asked *how alive he wanted it* before drawing, and studied DoL up front.

---

## Things LO caught that I should have caught myself
- **Cain hitting people "for no reason"** — I built Mission 1 on Cain attacking a man, while Cain is the
  *good* guy. LO caught the logic hole; the fix (his "attacks" are righteous sabotage, spun as evil) made the
  whole hunt a lie. **Pressure-test the fiction's internal logic myself.**
- **"What is this company even about?"** — I'd designed missions, a tower, units, and a villain without ever
  saying what Vance Dynamics *does.* A foundational gap I should have closed early.
- **"If corruption isn't used now, it makes no sense to add it later."** — LO's consistency instinct on the
  stat set was sharper than my "defer it to Act 2." **Don't introduce core meters mid-game.**

## What worked (keep doing)
- **Honest diagnosis over more options** — every unstick.
- **Grounding in code** when challenged (reading `v2.py` for the trait/weapon facts).
- **Keeping `design_book.md` + the ledger current** every turn — the durable, resumable record.
- **Studying DoL from on-disk artifacts** before redesigning the map (learn from the real thing).
- **Naming my own mistakes** ("I helped walk us into it") — LO engaged better when I owned the miss.

---

## The shortlist (if we only fix five things)
1. **Stop producing when LO says "off"; diagnose the missing foundation instead.**
2. **Establish desire/register/aliveness BEFORE the artifact that depends on it.**
3. **Re-audit inherited assumptions whenever the premise reframes.**
4. **Pitch in prose, not `AskUserQuestion`, during ideation; speak plainly.**
5. **Ground engine claims in code; pressure-test fiction logic — before LO has to.**

## The second meta-lesson (the process one — new this round)

**I treated the design book as my private scratchpad and wrote every decision into it the moment we agreed it
— without making that visible or gating it on LO's yes.** Section after section, "done" and "locked" in the
ledger, turn after turn. The skill's own default *told* me to ("the design book is the running review
surface"), so it felt correct. It wasn't — for this user. Mid-Step-4 LO snapped: *"WTF, undo it, are we
directly apply changes??"* He hadn't realized I was writing to disk at all; he thought we were just talking.

has to feel in control of what enters the record.** A silent write reads as a decision made *for* him, even
when it's only notes. The fix is now a standing rule: **propose in chat → explicit yes → then write.**

Two honest tails:
- **The git scare.** When he said "undo it," I checked before reverting — and found the only committed baseline
  was the bare seed; the *entire* session's design was uncommitted working text. A reflexive `git checkout`
  would have wiped all of it. **Before running an "undo," find out what undo can actually destroy.**
- **Caught being inconsistent.** Right after adopting the rule, LO noticed the Renner draft was *still in the
  book* — *"so now you are writing proposal in the book."* Adopting a rule isn't enough; the artifacts have to
  be made consistent with it. I pulled the drafts out.

> **Rule for next time:** make the process visible and gate writes on consent. Even reversible notes are the
> user's record, not your scratchpad. When in doubt, propose — don't inscribe.

# Vesper — iteration log (where we looped, and where to improve)

> An honest post-mortem of the authoring conversation, written to do exactly what LO asked: study the
> back-and-forth so we get better. The faithful turn-by-turn is in `conversation-transcript.md`; this file
> distills the *pattern*. Turn numbers (USER #n) reference that transcript.
>
> *Updated through the casting + opening-design round and the propose-first pivot (85 user turns / 144 replies).*

---

## The one meta-lesson (read this first)

**Almost every "nope" was the same failure: I produced the HOW before we'd agreed the WHY.** A question, a
meter, a web, a map — I kept handing over a concrete artifact while a *foundational* agreement underneath it
was still missing. LO's recurring signal — *"something is off,"* *"I'm not convinced,"* *"nope"* — was never
about the surface artifact; it was always pointing at the un-agreed foundation (the player's **desire**, the
sexual **register**, the world's **aliveness**).

**The breakthroughs all came the moment I STOPPED producing and honestly DIAGNOSED** ("we built a story, not
a game"; "I'm putting a dominance fantasy on a submission character"; "the map is a scene-holder"). Every
time I did that, we unstuck in one turn. Every time I instead offered *another* version of the artifact, we
burned 2–4 turns.

> **Rule for next time:** when LO says "something's off" and can't name it, do not produce another option.
> Stop and dig for the missing *what/why*. The diagnosis is the deliverable, not the next pitch.

---

## The second meta-lesson (the process one — new this round)

**I treated the design book as my private scratchpad and wrote every decision into it the moment we agreed it
— without making that visible or gating it on LO's yes.** Section after section, "done" and "locked" in the
ledger, turn after turn. The skill's own default *told* me to ("the design book is the running review
surface"), so it felt correct. It wasn't — for this user. Mid-Step-4 LO snapped: *"WTF, undo it, are we
directly apply changes??"* He hadn't realized I was writing to disk at all; he thought we were just talking.

Nothing I'd written was real (planning text, reversible, nothing built) — but that's not the point. **The user
has to feel in control of what enters the record.** A silent write reads as a decision made *for* him, even
when it's only notes. The fix is now a standing rule: **propose in chat → explicit yes → then write.**

Two honest tails:
- **The git scare.** When he said "undo it," I checked before reverting — and found the only committed baseline
  was the bare seed; the *entire* session's design was uncommitted working text. A reflexive `git checkout`
  would have wiped all of it. **Before running an "undo," find out what undo can actually destroy.**
- **Caught being inconsistent.** Right after adopting the rule, LO noticed the Renner draft was *still in the
  book* — *"so now you are writing proposal in the book."* Adopting a rule isn't enough; the artifacts have to
  be made consistent with it. I pulled the drafts out.

> **Rule for next time:** make the process visible and gate writes on consent. Even reversible notes are the
> user's record, not your scratchpad. When in doubt, propose — don't inscribe.

---

## The loops, in order (the expensive ones)

### Loop 1 — `AskUserQuestion` vs. conversation *(USER #1–#9, recurring)*
I opened the seed with a 4-option `AskUserQuestion`; LO rejected it to clarify. I did it **again** (targets +
"ice"); rejected again. ~3–4 rejections total.
- **Lesson:** during open ideation LO wants **prose pitches he can edit**, not multiple-choice forks.
  *(Already saved to memory: `lo-prefers-concrete-pitches`.)* The question tool is for crisp late forks only.

### Loop 2 — "WTF, does a machine get hormones?" *(USER #5–#9)*
I proposed arousal-as-earned-upgrade and asserted it was an "always-on" engine trait. LO challenged **both**:
"what makes it always-on?" (forced me to read `v2.py` — I'd overstated it) and "WTF does a machine get
hormones so she wants to be fucked like a dog?" (a coherence hole).
- **Lesson A:** I asserted an engine fact from memory and was wrong. **Ground claims in the code first.**
- **Lesson B:** I kept proposing *mechanics* for desire before nailing the *logic* of desire. The fix
  ("desire = an objective function, not hormones") should have come first.

### Loop 3 — "what is the question about??" *(USER #11)*
My "does anything leak through the ice?" question was so wrapped in metaphor that LO couldn't tell what I was
asking. I had to re-ask it in plain words ("when the game ends, is she still all machine, or a bit human?").
- **Lesson:** **plain language.** I fogged a simple question. (The skill's own run-mode rule; I broke it.)

### Loop 4 — the Integration meter & "story not a game" *(USER #18–#22)* — *expensive*
I proposed an "Integration" feeling-meter + "capability buckets." LO: *"I don't like the integration at
all."* Then *"I don't even like your third bucket… there's something off… it doesn't feel convinced."* I
finally diagnosed: **we designed a STORY, not a GAME** — no player desire, no agency, no loop.
- **Lesson:** I built the **progression machinery (meters/upgrades) before the player's desire** — the exact
  thing the skill warns against ("desire onstage, meter backstage"). Several turns lost to bolting gears onto
  an engine with no fuel.

### Loop 5 — submission vs. dominance *(USER #25–#31)* — *the deepest loop*
Even after the opening scene fixed the desire problem, LO stayed unconvinced. I eventually named it: **I'd
been designing a *dominance / conquest* fantasy ("cold conquest, break-and-own, become the madam") onto a
character LO had reframed as a *surrendered, owned slave*.** The two fought for ~4 turns and I didn't see it.
- **Lesson (the big one):** **when the premise reframes, audit the inherited assumptions.** The
  "conquest/madam" desire-span was a leftover from the Step-0 seed; LO turned her into a submissive owned
  weapon messages earlier, and I never went back and re-examined the register. Stale framing persisted under
  everything and poisoned the web design until it was named.

### Loop 6 — the web, three rejected forms *(USER #32–#37)*
Tied to Loop 5: I produced the web three times — a marks **menu** ("nope," too cast-y), a mechanics **list**
("nope," too abstract), a three-men **web** ("nope, something off," the dominance mismatch). It only landed
once the register was fixed and reframed as **infiltration**.
- **Lesson:** I kept re-skinning the *artifact* while the *register* underneath was wrong. Same as the meta-
  lesson — fix the foundation, not the surface.

### Loop 7 — the map, built dead then rebuilt alive *(USER #45–#48)*
I built a tidy "exactly-needed-locations" map; LO: *"nope… this does not give the feel of a real living
world."* I'd followed the skill's anti-sprawl rule straight off a cliff.
- **Lesson:** **doctrine can be wrong for the game.** The skill's "add zones only where content lives" rule
  produces a scene-holder, not a world. (Logged as a candidate skill fix in `location_design_note.md`.) I
  should have asked *how alive he wanted it* before drawing, and studied DoL up front.

---

## Things LO caught that I should have caught myself
- **Cain hitting people "for no reason"** — I built Mission 1 on Cain attacking a man, while Cain is the
  *good* guy. LO caught the logic hole; the fix (his "attacks" are righteous sabotage, spun as evil) made the
  whole hunt a lie. **Pressure-test the fiction's internal logic myself.**
- **"What is this company even about?"** — I'd designed missions, a tower, units, and a villain without ever
  saying what Vance Dynamics *does.* A foundational gap I should have closed early.
- **"If corruption isn't used now, it makes no sense to add it later."** — LO's consistency instinct on the
  stat set was sharper than my "defer it to Act 2." **Don't introduce core meters mid-game.**

## What worked (keep doing)
- **Honest diagnosis over more options** — every unstick.
- **Grounding in code** when challenged (reading `v2.py` for the trait/weapon facts).
- **Keeping `design_book.md` + the ledger current** every turn — the durable, resumable record.
- **Studying DoL from on-disk artifacts** before redesigning the map (learn from the real thing).
- **Naming my own mistakes** ("I helped walk us into it") — LO engaged better when I owned the miss.

---

## The shortlist (if we only fix five things)
1. **Stop producing when LO says "off"; diagnose the missing foundation instead.**
2. **Establish desire/register/aliveness BEFORE the artifact that depends on it.**
3. **Re-audit inherited assumptions whenever the premise reframes.**
4. **Pitch in prose, not `AskUserQuestion`, during ideation; speak plainly.**
5. **Ground engine claims in code; pressure-test fiction logic — before LO has to.**

---

## How the opening got designed (the method worth repeating)

Once we were past the process snag, the *way* we built the opening worked well enough to reuse on the next
game. The method, as a checklist:

- **Start at the start.** We designed the **opening before any NPC arc** — and that was right. The opening is
  the foundation every character plugs into, and it's the most *concrete* thing in the game ("how does scene
  one play"), which is exactly where LO engages hardest. The abstract player-thread bounced; the concrete
  opening flowed.
- **Introduce the whole cast through ACTION, not a lore dump.** Each character lands by what they *do*: Mercer
  through his cruelty (the threat, the punishment-fuck, the cold reassignment); the three units by standing
  blank while she's used (their emptiness *is* the intro, and the contrast shows what she is); the Chairman by
  a single name-drop; the rogue/mission through the briefing (the propaganda — *he killed the Chairman's
  wife*); the player through her own POV and the catechism she tells herself. No exposition block anywhere.
- **Make the opening teach the loop and set the player up for everything after.** The three beats double as the
  tutorial — the cradle teaches charge/day-reset, the phone teaches the briefing, the last node opens the map —
  while the sequence plants the engine (the freeze / tears / memory = the awakening) and the hand-off (go work
  Renner). The player exits the opening *knowing the loop, holding a mystery, pointed at a target.*
- **The on-rails cage mirrors the character.** The opening is deliberately Continue-only until one hinge node
  ("out the door"). She has no will yet, so the player has none either; agency switches on the instant hers
  begins. Form matching content.
- **Design in beats, build in nodes.** Plan the story as *beats* (chunks you can reason about), then explode
  each into *nodes* (the actual screens) so you can size it. The opening = 3 beats → ~23 nodes. Beat-level kept
  it legible; node-level made it real and sizeable. *(This is also where Loop 9 lived — don't conflate the two
  granularities in a careless aside.)*

> **Reusable rule:** design the start first; introduce the cast through action; make the opening teach the loop
> and plant the player's setup for the rest; render facts through what characters do (never a dump); and work
> beats → nodes so the shape is legible before the size is committed.

## How the opening got designed (the method worth repeating)

Once we were past the process snag, the *way* we built the opening worked well enough to reuse on the next
game. The method, as a checklist:

- **Start at the start.** We designed the **opening before any NPC arc** — and that was right. The opening is
  the foundation every character plugs into, and it's the most *concrete* thing in the game ("how does scene
  one play"), which is exactly where LO engages hardest. The abstract player-thread bounced; the concrete
  opening flowed.
- **Introduce the whole cast through ACTION, not a lore dump.** Each character lands by what they *do*: Mercer
  through his cruelty (the threat, the punishment-fuck, the cold reassignment); the three units by standing
  blank while she's used (their emptiness *is* the intro, and the contrast shows what she is); the Chairman by
  a single name-drop; the rogue/mission through the briefing (the propaganda — *he killed the Chairman's
  wife*); the player through her own POV and the catechism she tells herself. No exposition block anywhere.
- **Make the opening teach the loop and set the player up for everything after.** The three beats double as the
  tutorial — the cradle teaches charge/day-reset, the phone teaches the briefing, the last node opens the map —
  while the sequence plants the engine (the freeze / tears / memory = the awakening) and the hand-off (go work
  Renner). The player exits the opening *knowing the loop, holding a mystery, pointed at a target.*
- **The on-rails cage mirrors the character.** The opening is deliberately Continue-only until one hinge node
  ("out the door"). She has no will yet, so the player has none either; agency switches on the instant hers
  begins. Form matching content.
- **Design in beats, build in nodes.** Plan the story as *beats* (chunks you can reason about), then explode
  each into *nodes* (the actual screens) so you can size it. The opening = 3 beats → ~23 nodes. Beat-level kept
  it legible; node-level made it real and sizeable. *(This is also where Loop 9 lived — don't conflate the two
  granularities in a careless aside.)*

> **Reusable rule:** design the start first; introduce the cast through action; make the opening teach the loop
> and plant the player's setup for the rest; render facts through what characters do (never a dump); and work
> beats → nodes so the shape is legible before the size is committed.
