196	- **Bastien's** *(pawn-front / back room)* — *Job:* **Mission 2** anchor (the dealer, Cain's supply). [reachable]
197	- **The Anchor** *(dive bar)* — *Job:* **Mission 1** anchor (Renner drowns his guilt here; she works him) +
198	  ambient leads. [reachable]
199	- **The Facility (ruins)** — the evil Vance asset-facility Cain destroyed. *Job:* **Mission 1** investigation —
200	  the first dread-place. [reachable]
201	- **🔒 The Site** — Cain's just-abandoned hideout; the **chip**. **Locked** (*"you don't know where he went —
202	  yet"*) until enough leads. [locked → unlocks on leads]
203	- *(Marrow's lost lab — buried under The Reach; Act-2, seeded.)*
204	
205	**What makes it LIVE (systems, not empty rooms):**
206	- **People on schedules** — targets *move* (Calloway: office by day / the Eyrie some nights; Bastien: his
207	  front after dark; Renner: the Anchor evenings); ambient NPCs fill the streets. You *catch* them — the city
208	  has its own clock.
209	- **Ambient street events** — the three street hubs (Plaza / Strip / Waterfront) fire random encounters: city
210	  life, a surveillance sweep, a glitch, an opportunity. Life you didn't trigger.
211	- **The world remembers** — covers build reputations, surveillance notices, word travels. A *light* reactive
212	  layer (the "alive" ingredient the first map lacked).
213	
214	**Naming (noir, consistent):** owned/private = possessive (*Mercer's Penthouse · Wren's Room · the Cradle ·
215	Bastien's*); public = bare/branded nouns (*Spire Plaza · The Eyrie · Mirage · The Cordon · The Anchor · The
216	Waterfront · The Facility · The Site*); district headers in caps.
217	
218	**Engine tree (IDs):**
219	- `loc_spire` → spire_plaza · vance_tower (→ atrium · wren_floor → wren_room → cradle · lab · units_quarters · penthouse) · vance_securities · the_eyrie
220	- `loc_midcity` → the_strip · mirage · the_cordon · the_long_hour
221	- `loc_reach` → the_waterfront · bastiens · the_anchor · facility_ruins · the_site🔒
222	- districts linked by travel (spire ⇄ midcity ⇄ reach); fast-travel once known.
223	
224	---
225	
226	## Top-level design (Step 2) — the engine, the web & the economy  *(in progress)*
227	
228	**The fantasy register (the thing we kept getting wrong, now logical):**
229	- **Inside = submission.** She's an owned slave; dominance there makes no sense.
230	- **Outside = infiltration.** She can't appear as what she is, so she takes a **cover identity** and slips
231	  into a target's life. The register (caretaker / submissive / domme) is **whatever gets her in** — his
232	  weakness is the door. Not her nature; her tool.
233	
234	**The secret weapon (LOCKED — the key that fuses fantasy + mission):** she must *mean* the sex (her pleasure
235	powers it); at **his climax inside her** she passes a fluid that gives her **full control.** **In-game (no
236	real timer):** the climax routes to a **control canvas** — she questions / commands / drains him (the
237	extraction) — and when it ends, ~10 fiction-minutes have passed and **he remembers nothing** (the mark wakes
238	clean, reusable). She wins by *submitting.* Never used on the boss in Phase 1 — only targets. The control
239	canvas is the **payoff scene of every infiltration.**
240	
241	**The loop (Inside ↔ Outside):**
242	> **Inside:** serve Mercer (sex + chores), take the order, charge (memories leak). → **Outside:** take a
243	> cover, slip into the target's life, become what he needs, then deploy the weapon and drain him. → **Back
244	> inside:** serve, charge, dread climbs. → next target… → the trail → the site → **the chip → the fracture.**
245	
246	**The hunt is a LIE from beat one.** Cain is good; the company *spins* his righteous sabotage as "vicious
247	rogue attacks." So the player's driving want — *catch the monster* — is built on a lie that **inverts** at
248	the reveal (kill → maybe love). Every mission quietly shows the opposite of the briefing.
249	
250	**The Phase-1 web — three infiltrations → the chip:**
251	1. **Renner (the way in).** Cain destroyed his **evil facility**; he's covering what it really did. *Caretaker
252	   cover.* → what Cain took **+** the first crack in "evil rogue." Opens threads 2 and 3.
253	2. **Bastien (supply).** Cain's gear comes through dealers like him. *Submissive cover.* → where Cain's been.
254	3. **Calloway (the file).** The insider with the dossier; secretly wants to submit. *Domme cover.* → Cain's
255	   last movements **+** "the company's hiding something."
256	- **Order:** Renner first; then Bastien / Calloway in **either order** (player's freedom); enough pieces →
257	  **the site** → Cain's gone but **left the chip for her** → first memory bleeds → **Phase 1 ends.**
258	
259	**The economy (formalized):**
260	- **Not survival rent — the pressure is the leash + the cost of going off-book.** Phase 1: provided-for,
261	  **deliberately light** (a kept slave needs nothing; small spend to reach a target). Act 2: she funds her
262	  *own* off-book agenda — the economy *ignites* with her independence. Endgame: hunted — survival-war.
263	- **One wallet (credits).** Earned by working marks (= content). **Anti-grind** via the open web.
264	- **Sinks (wanted buys):** capability upgrades · disguise/clothing (the covers) · bribes/access (buy the way
265	  to the next node — the economy as connective tissue) · (Act 2) off-book survival.
266	- **Charge** paces the day and becomes a **vulnerability** when hunted (powering down = exposed).
267	- **Fail-state (§8):** YES — neglect jobs / let the malfunction show / expose yourself → the leash tightens
268	  (monitoring → enforcers → the hunt). Declared on purpose. **Chip-fragments are not economy** (mystery spine).
269	
270	**The stat set (LOCKED — every stat gates real content; nothing decorative):**
271	- **Money (credits)** — the one wallet. Gates gear / disguise / bribes / upgrades.
272	- **Charge** (the engine's `energy`, reskinned) — paces the day (costs on actions/travel), refilled at the
273	  cradle; a vulnerability once she's hunted.
274	- **Capabilities / upgrades = INVENTORY items** — each upgrade is a thing she owns and installs (a buyable
275	  loadout; content gates on *owns-it*). Not a meter.
276	- **Chip / memories = INVENTORY items** — recovered fragments are collectibles (recovering one fires its
277	  memory beat; a *memories* view holds them). Not a meter.
278	- **Per-target lock = relation + corruption** (the target's own built-in traits; exact use set per character
279	  at casting, Step 4):
280	  - **relation** = the **infiltration** — embedded under a cover, works for him, he trusts her (*"I'm in your
281	    world"*). Built by the work/trust grind.
282	  - **corruption** = the **seduction** — how far she's hooked / compromised him (*"I'm in your head and your
283	    bed"*). Built by the seduction grind; extends smoothly into Act 2 (*hooked → owned*). **Replaces npc
284	    arousal (removed).**
285	  - Both high → he beds her → the weapon (climax → control canvas → drain).
286	- **Deliberately NONE:** her arousal · a feeling/"humanity" meter · a heat/suspicion meter. The company's
287	  crackdown / the leash is handled by **story beats + flags**, not a tracked bar.
288	
289	**Scope (LO):** building **Phase 1 only** for now — up to the chip / the fracture. Phase 1 ends on a
290	**cliffhanger** (the fracture into Act 2), *not* a frontier-plateau — correct for a slice toward the whole.
291	
292	**PARKED (known open questions, not skipped — Act-2 design):** **pacing/frontier** (the kill-or-love peak +
293	the livable post-game plateau + the endless-sandbox signpost). Phase-1 pacing is already carried by the web
294	(the mission loop + escalating dread → the fracture).
295	
296	**Next:** Step 2b — the map (the Phase-1 location graph).
297	
298	---
299	
300	## Casting (Step 3) — every NPC has a role + a hook
301	
302	> Most of this cast was decided across Steps 0–2; this section *formalizes* it — role, one-line hook,
303	> fantasy lane, depth, arc-shape, and the node each core NPC holds in the loop — so Step 4 designs each arc
304	> against a clear job, not from scratch. Phase-1 names locked; lighter/seeded names marked *(placeholder)*.
305	
306	**Coverage (the cascade runs):** pressure source = **Mercer** (the leash) · corrupting on-ramp = **Mercer**
307	(he issues every mission = the loop) · core targets = **Renner / Bastien / Calloway** (three distinct lanes) ·
308	late-act pressure = **Mercer tightening** + **Dr. Pell flagging the glitches** (escalates toward the hunt).
309	The desire span (submission→agency) is delivered across the three covers: **caretaker / submissive / domme**,
310	the last a first taste of the user she's becoming.
311	
312	| NPC | role(s) | hook (dynamic · charge · want) | lane | depth | arc-shape | machine node |
313	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
314	| **Mercer** | pressure source · on-ramp · the inside relationship · late-act pressure | Your owner and handler — fucks you on a whim, hands you his chores, knows every secret you have; wants his prize weapon flawless and obedient (his own standing rides on you). | dominant / owner | core (not a Phase-1 conquest) | **owner/authority — flag-driven** (the leash + tightening danger; no relation/corruption lock) | **inside hub** — issues the order, consumes the service, gates the day; turns "back inside" into "next target out" |
315	| **Renner** | core target (Mission 1, the way in) | The man who ran the facility Cain burned — now a guilt-drunk wreck at the Anchor who just wants it to stop; you come as comfort and he clings. | nurturing / caretaker | core | **infiltration — relation + corruption**; personal spine = guilt → dependence | **entry node** — draining him opens Bastien + Calloway and lands the first crack in "evil rogue" |
316	| **Bastien** | core target (Mission 2, supply) | The docks dealer who supplies Cain — a smug fixer sure he's using every new face; you play the eager newcomer he thinks he's breaking in. | transactional / underworld | core | **infiltration — relation + corruption**; spine = greed → control (he's the user who gets used) | **supply node** — drain yields *where Cain's been operating* + underworld access (parallel to Calloway) |
317	| **Calloway** | core target (Mission 3, the file) | The company man running the Cain-hunt — rigid, controlling, privately starving to be made to kneel; you're his new assistant and his secret is the door. | dominant / power-flip (**she** runs the register) | core | **infiltration — relation + corruption**; spine = control → release | **file node** — the richest source; drain unlocks **the site** ("the company's hiding something") |
318	| **Cain** | the hunt's object · the reserved end (kill-or-love) · truth-bearer | The "vicious rogue" you're sent to kill — actually the one who loved you, at war with the company that owns you, leaving you a trail home. | the one reserved warmth (mostly deferred) | core to the STORY, **light on-screen in Phase 1** | **mystery/reveal spine** (chip fragments + inverting briefings; no lock) | **convergence** — the three target-nodes feed leads that point at him → the site → the chip → the fracture |
319	| **Dr. Pell** *(placeholder)* | seeded Act-2 origin/upgrade thread · soft late-act pressure | The company roboticist who keeps you running — the one man who could read your build and realize what you are; for now he just notices the readings drift. | (not a desire target in P1) | light / seeded | **thread NPC** (flag) + upgrade vendor | **upgrade sink** (capability items) + the **glitch-flag** that feeds the tightening leash |
320	| **Vega · Lyra · Nova** (the units) | mirror / dread — the company's ideal tool (no self) | The company's own three operatives — complete machines, sleeker and stronger and *empty*; better hardware than you, no human base, no real feeling. The proof of what the company wishes you were. | (dread mirror, no desire) | light / seeded — **opening mention only** | **ambient dread** (named, no arc) | none in P1 (Act-2) |
321	| **Sol** *(placeholder)* | ambient anchor — city-life · leads-color | The Long Hour's bartender who's seen everything and asks nothing — the one face in the city who treats you like a regular, not an owner or a mark. | light warmth, no conquest | light island | **leads-color** (no lock) | none (deliberately — the "world beyond the missions") |
322	
323	### Rough sketches + cross-NPC threads
324	- **Mercer** — opens the game (his bed). Dispatches Renner, then opens Bastien/Calloway; debriefs and uses
325	  her on every return. As chip fragments surface, he and **Pell** start noticing the glitches — the leash
326	  visibly tightens toward the fracture. He's never the weapon's target in Phase 1 (that's the Act-2 seed:
327	  the day she turns it on him, used→user). *Thread:* he + Pell are the **two who can catch her.**
328	- **Renner** — at the Anchor, evenings. Worked as comfort → confesses fragments of what the facility really
329	  *did* → beds her → control canvas → drains: what Cain took, why, and the first wrong-note (Cain *freed*
330	  people). *Thread:* the facility is where the **units** trail back to (Act-2) — what it built.
331	- **Bastien** — pawn-front after dark, back room once trusted. Plays submissive-newcomer → gains access →
332	  beds him → control canvas → drains Cain's movements + supply routes. *Thread:* his docks turf overlaps
333	  Cain's world; a lead here can point at **the site.**
334	- **Calloway** — Vance Securities by day, the Eyrie some nights. Hired as PA → finds the craving → flips to
335	  **domme** → he submits → control canvas → drains the dossier (Cain's last trail + the cover-up). The domme
336	  register **foreshadows her awakening.** *Thread:* he's inside the Spire, so this brushes **Mercer** and the
337	  company's surveillance — the riskiest infiltration (working under her owners' noses).
338	- **Cain** — present in Phase 1 only as: the company's **briefings** (the lie), the **wrong-notes** each
339	  target reveals (the inversion), and the **site** (he's gone, left the chip *for her, by name*). The chip is
340	  the first time the hunt turns personal — he's been reaching for *her*, not running.
341	- **Dr. Pell** — at the Lab. She visits for maintenance/upgrades; over Phase 1 her readings drift and he
342	  flags it. *Thread:* the Act-2 door to "what she is"; could become ally or threat.
343	- **Vega · Lyra · Nova (the units)** — established at the **opening only**: the company's three other
344	  operatives, complete machines that do the same work she does with none of the spark. Named so the world has
345	  peers in it, but they don't recur in Phase 1. *Thread (Act-2):* they're the company's pure-machine line —
346	  living proof it can't make Marrow's soul, which is why it can't replace her and why the Chairman needs her.
347	- **Sol** — the Long Hour. Just *there* — remembers her, trades gossip, colors a lead. No arc, no conquest;
348	  the small proof the city isn't built only for the missions.
349	
350	### Cast locked (your calls)
351	1. **Cain is physically offstage for all of Phase 1.** His presence escalates instead (the lie → wrong-notes
352	   → "he asked about you by name" → the chip he left *for you*); the chip at the fracture is the first real
353	   contact. The kill-or-love face-to-face is saved whole for Act 2.
354	2. **The units are complete machines (no human base, no real feeling), named individually — Vega, Lyra,
355	   Nova.** They're the company's own field operatives; **mentioned only at the opening** (peers who set up the
356	   Act-2 mirror), not recurring in Phase 1.
357	3. **Sol (the bartender) stays, light** — the lived-in, world-beyond-the-missions texture.
358	
359	*(Placeholder names still open to rename: **Dr. Pell**, **Sol**.)*
360	
361	---
362	
363	## The opening (design) — the on-rails cage, then the first free step
364	
365	> The agreed opening sequence. **Mostly on-rails** (Continue → Continue) across three beats — the cage —
366	> until one hinge node where the city opens. **~23 nodes** before she reaches Renner. Its job: show her as the
367	> most owned thing in the building, introduce the cast through *action* (never a lore dump), and hide three
368	> cracks the player sees and she doesn't. Everything she believes about herself is the lie the game takes apart.
369	> *(Beat = a chunk of story; node = one screen the player clicks. One beat → many nodes. Supersedes the early
370	> "bed → cradle" opening sketch.)*
371	
372	**Shape:** Beat 1 (office) → Beat 2 (night) → Beat 3 (morning) → *out the door* → the Anchor / Renner.
373	**The hinge:** the final morning node — *out the door* — flips the game from on-rails to open (the city map +
374	real choices switch on). The twenty-odd Continue screens before it are the point: the first free step has to
375	*feel* like something after being owned.
376	
377	### Beat 1 — The office (~12 nodes) — the punishment + the setup
378	1. **The line-up** — she and the three units stand before Mercer; the failed op hangs in the air.
379	2. **The accusation** — they had the rogue, she froze, he's gone. *(introduces the rogue + her freeze)*
380	3. **The threat** — he threatens to scrap her; the units stand blank. *(flavor choice: beg / silent / explain — same outcome)*
381	4. **She begs** — her surrender on display; she pleads to keep serving.
382	5. **The verdict** — too valuable to destroy ("the Chairman's investment" — *names the Chairman + her worth*); punishment instead.
383	6. **The punishment, set up** — he'll use her, here, now, in front of them.
384	7–9. **The punishment (~3 nodes, flexes ±)** — he takes her → the act (explicit, her body answering) → the units watching, blank, while *she* feels it. *(the "she feels, they don't" mirror)*
385	10. **Gratitude** — she thanks him; the degradation she accepts.
386	11. **The reassignment** — names Vega / Lyra / Nova to the head-on hunt; gives *her* the inside job ("useless with a gun, but…"); frames the mission: *the rogue murdered the Chairman's wife, enemy of the company and the world.*
387	12. **Dismissed** — out of the office → the night.
388	- **Introduces:** Mercer (cruel owner) · the three units (perfect, empty — her opposite) · the Chairman (named, the power above) · the rogue / mission (the "monster") · her (the owned asset who failed).
389	- **Hidden crack:** the freeze = the **first glitch.** Everyone reads it as a malfunction.
390	
391	### Beat 2 — The night (~7 nodes) — the cradle, fully linear
392	1. **The walk back** — through the Tower to her own floor and room.
393	2. **The cradle** — she powers into the charging cradle; the reset ritual. *(the cradle = charge / save / start-of-day)*
394	3. **The tears** — her body cries; she can't explain the water; reads it as a fault to hide.
395	4. **The leak** — a memory fragment surfaces (a face, a sound, a name she doesn't know), then gone.
396	5. **The catechism** — she recites what she's told she is: *saved by the company and the Chairman, owes them everything, exists to obey.*
397	6. **The power** — her gift (control of a man the instant he finishes inside her, company-given) — and the odd fact it's **never** worked on the boss, never questioned.
398	7. **Power-down** — she promises to do better; powers down. *(the retreat into the leash)*
399	- **Introduces:** who she *thinks* she is (the lie). **Plants:** the awakening (tears + memory) + the boss-immunity mystery.
400	- **(No flavor choices — kept fully on-rails by design.)**
401	
402	### Beat 3 — The morning (~4 nodes) — the task, then the city opens
403	1. **Power-up** — she wakes in the cradle, charged, a new day. *(the day-cycle / morning start)*
404	2. **The briefing** — a dossier waiting on her phone. *(the phone)*
405	3. **The tip** — what happened (a facility burned), why her (Renner knows the trail), what she can do (get close, the gift), where (the Anchor).
406	4. **Out the door** *(the hinge)* — she takes a cover and steps out of the Tower for the first time → **the city opens.** → the Anchor / meet Renner.
407	- **Introduces:** the loop (out → get close → drain → bring back the lead) + the cover/disguise + moving the map. **Hands off to:** Renner.
408	
409	### Craft notes (how it must be written)
410	- **Render, don't dump.** Facts arrive through what she *does* (the charging ritual, the briefing) and the catechism she tells herself — never a backstory wall. The true origin stays underwater (iceberg); the memory is a **fragment**, never a clean flashback.
411	- **Crying = malfunction.** She feels *nothing but the sex* — so the tears are a thing her body does that she can't explain and would hide. The player sees grief; she sees a fault. (Same as the freeze.)
412	- **Belief vs. truth.** Write her self-concept *straight* (machine, saved, owes them, obeys) and **never confirm it.** The gap between what she says and what the player suspects is the engine.
413	- **The cage mirrors her.** On-rails = she has no will yet, so the player doesn't either. Agency switches on with her first free step.
414	
415	### Parked mysteries (Chekhov's guns — planted here, paid off later, not resolved)
416	- **The Chairman's wife.** The "rogue murdered her" story is the company's **lie / propaganda** (it keeps Cain good). What *really* happened to her is a later reveal. *(Truth: TBD.)*
417	- **Why the weapon fails on the boss.** *Candidate (not locked):* the weapon needs a *self* to fire (her own pleasure / will) — and in total surrender to Mercer there's no "her" present, so nothing triggers it. The day it finally works on him = the day she's awake enough to *be* someone (wires the Act-2 used→user turn).
418	- **The Chairman's motive.** *Optional seed:* his hunger for a deathless, *feeling* body is **grief** — he lost her and will burn the world to never lose anyone again.
419	
420	---

# Vesper — Design Book

> The user's review surface. This is **intent in plain language** — the engine/TOML is the faithful
> translation of what's written here. Grown one section per pipeline step.
>
> Working title: **Vesper** (also the PC's buried true name — hidden in plain sight; rename freely).
> Book revision 11 (the opening designed; Step 4 continuing).

---

## World setup

**POV.** Female PC. The arc is **awakening from total surrender** — an owned, will-less slave slowly growing
a self the company never gave her. Her sexual register is **contextual, not fixed:** *inside* the company
she's a submissive slave (dominance there makes no sense); *outside* on missions she wears a cover and plays
whatever a target needs. The **dominance / taking-control** is where she's *headed* as she wakes up
(used → user) — earned, not the start.

**What she is (the core — read this first):**
- **Half-human, not a pure machine.** Marrow's breakthrough was building his creations on a *living human
  base* — that's *why* they can truly feel. She (and Cain) are human-derived. Her human memory is wiped; she
  believes she's only a company machine. *(Whose human she was stays buried — surfaced only as far as it
  feeds the central reveal, never a forked subplot.)*
- **Total surrender — no will of her own.** She believes she exists only to serve. Inside the company she's a
  **slave** — everyone uses her, the **boss owns her** (sex *and* chores). She has no motive of her own; her
  motive *is* the company's. The whole game is her motive peeling away from theirs.
- **She loves sex — it's the ONE thing she feels.** Everything else is blank. This is *not* contentment;
  it's the opposite — they hollowed her out and left a single spark. A slave who only comes alive while
  she's being fucked. (And it's the **fuel for her weapon** — below.) The chip is the first hint there was
  once a whole person who felt *more than this.*
- **Her secret weapon — the sex-weapon (LOCKED).** She has to *mean* the sex (her own pleasure powers it).
  At the moment **he climaxes inside her,** she passes him a fluid that puts her in **full control of him.**
  Used only on **targets** — never the boss (she stays surrendered to him); it's the one thing that's *hers.*
  **In-game (no real timer):** his climax routes to a **control canvas** where she questions and commands him
  (the extraction = both *drain* and *command*); when that canvas ends, ~10 minutes have passed in the
  fiction and **he remembers nothing** — he wakes clean, so a mark can be reused. His own orgasm is the key
  that hands her the controls. *(Act-2 seed: the day she turns it on Mercer, the used becomes the user.)*

**Where she lives — Vance Dynamics & the Tower (LOCKED).** The company isn't an office she commutes to; it's a
**vertical arcology where everyone lives** — staff, assets, the boss — a total institution and a literal cage.
The business runs in three layers (matching the reveal architecture):
- **Public face:** a prestige **robotics/AI megacorp** (automation, security, cybernetics) — the legit
  storefront that explains the labs, the scientists, the thousands of employees, most of whom never see what's
  underneath.
- **The real business — *ownership*.** It uses human-derived **assets** like Wren to run the world's most
  powerful intelligence-and-control operation: it *owns* the powerful by knowing the secrets it extracts.
  **The missions ARE the core business** — every honeypot is the company owning another powerful man.
- **The deepest secret (Act-2):** the asset program is really the Chairman's machine for his own immortality.

The theme with a logo on it: **a company whose whole trade is owning people** — literally (people remade into
tools) and figuratively (the powerful owned through their secrets) — and a protagonist who is *a person it
owns, waking up.* Wren is one of several assets, and the irreplaceable **original** among them (see Cast).

**The fantasy (clears the 3-part bar) — designer's full-arc view:**
> You're an owned half-human weapon who feels nothing but the sex she's used for. Inside, you're the
> company's slave; outside, you slip into powerful men's lives under a false face and drain them while they
> think they're using you. They send you to hunt an "evil" rogue — who is the one person who ever loved you.
> Claw back the self they erased, climb to the man who's owned it all for generations, and at the end decide:
> **kill the one waiting there, or love him.**

- **POV-fit** ✓ — female-PC reclamation; the reversal is **owned slave → the one who owns.**
- **Sharp charge** ✓ — **transformation** (an erased person waking), **submission→conquest** (used tool that
  becomes the user), and a **cold taboo** (a hollow slave who feels only the sex, with a hidden weapon in it).
- **Two-act shape** ✓ — Act 1: surrendered tool; infiltrate and drain men to hunt the "evil" rogue; the
  first crack (Phase 1). Act 2: dig in secret; climb Vance; recover herself; reach the Chairman and the
  truth — turn the weapon on her owners, face the rogue. Kill-or-love.

**Desire span (declared) — an ARC from submission to agency.**
- **Targets:** **mostly men** — the powerful men she's sent to infiltrate.
- **Phase 1 / Act 1 register:** **submission.** Inside = owned slave. Outside = infiltration, where she plays
  whatever the cover/target needs (caretaker / submissive / domme — the register flexes *logically* per man).
- **The arc:** used → user. The **dominance, the break-and-own conquest** is **earned late**, as she
  awakens — never the Phase-1 register.
- **Feeling:** she feels only the sex. Emotional warmth (caring/love) stays reserved for **Cain at the very
  end** — kill-or-love.

**The hidden backstory (iceberg — LOCKED; never dumped, only reconstructed):**
1. **Dr. Elias Marrow** cracked synthetic consciousness — **human-derived** (built on a living human base;
   that's why it truly *feels*). He built **Cain first** (half-human; he feels).
2. Marrow built **her second, the same way — a companion *for Cain*.** Made to feel, to be loved.
3. Realizing what the company would do with feeling beings, Marrow chose **total erasure** (Cain kills
   Marrow, then destroys the unfinished girl, then ends himself) — to deny the company. Cain agreed, out of
   love and duty.
4. **The company interrupted.** Cain killed Marrow, then they hit him mid-plan; he fought, **lost, ran** —
   and they **seized her, unfinished,** wiped her memory, made her a weapon, left only the body's pleasure.
5. Now they aim **her — the one Cain failed to save — at killing *him*.** She hunts the only person who ever
   tried to spare her this. Cain has warred on the company ever since, partly *because they took her.*

**The generational villain (LOCKED).** **The Chairman — Aldous Vance** — never died; a man clinging to life
through technology, already part-machine. He wants Marrow's human-derived soul to become a **human-machine
fusion:** true immortality *and* a self that still feels. **The half-human secret is what he's killing to
get.** She's the **working prototype** (they chained her feeling to use her now, harvest the soul later).
**Inverse mirror:** she's a half-human reaching back toward herself; he's a human shedding humanity for
permanence. The **Act-2 conquest target** (she may end *owning* Vance), kept distinct from Cain's kill-or-love
fork. Remote and mythic — she doesn't reach him until late.

**The reveal architecture (LOCKED):**
- **The backstory is the well, not the pour.** She reconstructs the truth as she reconstructs the **chip** —
  her remembering and the player's understanding are one act. The mystery is the plot's desire ladder.
- **Facts locked to her, dread a step ahead.** The player senses the wrongness before she'll admit it.
- **The masks rhyme with the mystery.** She wears a false self for every mission while her *real* self is the
  one thing they erased — so the infiltration theme *is* the awakening theme; the chip is her true identity
  surfacing under all the covers.
- **Reveal channels:** chip restoration · glitch-intrusions (charging) · how others treat her (Cain *knows*
  her) · the body (pleasure she can't explain).
- **Hide the origin, not the nature.**

**Player.** **Fixed identity — not player-named** (Wren / buried Vesper). In-world disguises are content.

**Systems:** **Phone** YES · **Clothing** YES (disguise + the covers) · **Money/economy** YES (resources, not
rent) · **Customization** minimal / no creator.

## Top-level design (Step 2) — the engine, the web & the economy  *(in progress)*

**The fantasy register (the thing we kept getting wrong, now logical):**
- **Inside = submission.** She's an owned slave; dominance there makes no sense.
- **Outside = infiltration.** She can't appear as what she is, so she takes a **cover identity** and slips
  into a target's life. The register (caretaker / submissive / domme) is **whatever gets her in** — his
  weakness is the door. Not her nature; her tool.

**The secret weapon (LOCKED — the key that fuses fantasy + mission):** she must *mean* the sex (her pleasure
powers it); at **his climax inside her** she passes a fluid that gives her **full control.** **In-game (no
real timer):** the climax routes to a **control canvas** — she questions / commands / drains him (the
extraction) — and when it ends, ~10 fiction-minutes have passed and **he remembers nothing** (the mark wakes
clean, reusable). She wins by *submitting.* Never used on the boss in Phase 1 — only targets. The control
canvas is the **payoff scene of every infiltration.**

**The loop (Inside ↔ Outside):**
> **Inside:** serve Mercer (sex + chores), take the order, charge (memories leak). → **Outside:** take a
> cover, slip into the target's life, become what he needs, then deploy the weapon and drain him. → **Back
> inside:** serve, charge, dread climbs. → next target… → the trail → the site → **the chip → the fracture.**

**The hunt is a LIE from beat one.** Cain is good; the company *spins* his righteous sabotage as "vicious
rogue attacks." So the player's driving want — *catch the monster* — is built on a lie that **inverts** at
the reveal (kill → maybe love). Every mission quietly shows the opposite of the briefing.

**The Phase-1 web — three infiltrations → the chip:**
1. **Renner (the way in).** Cain destroyed his **evil facility**; he's covering what it really did. *Caretaker
   cover.* → what Cain took **+** the first crack in "evil rogue." Opens threads 2 and 3.
2. **Bastien (supply).** Cain's gear comes through dealers like him. *Submissive cover.* → where Cain's been.
3. **Calloway (the file).** The insider with the dossier; secretly wants to submit. *Domme cover.* → Cain's
   last movements **+** "the company's hiding something."
- **Order:** Renner first; then Bastien / Calloway in **either order** (player's freedom); enough pieces →
  **the site** → Cain's gone but **left the chip for her** → first memory bleeds → **Phase 1 ends.**

**The economy (formalized):**
- **Not survival rent — the pressure is the leash + the cost of going off-book.** Phase 1: provided-for,
  **deliberately light** (a kept slave needs nothing; small spend to reach a target). Act 2: she funds her
  *own* off-book agenda — the economy *ignites* with her independence. Endgame: hunted — survival-war.
- **One wallet (credits).** Earned by working marks (= content). **Anti-grind** via the open web.
- **Sinks (wanted buys):** capability upgrades · disguise/clothing (the covers) · bribes/access (buy the way
  to the next node — the economy as connective tissue) · (Act 2) off-book survival.
- **Charge** paces the day and becomes a **vulnerability** when hunted (powering down = exposed).
- **Fail-state (§8):** YES — neglect jobs / let the malfunction show / expose yourself → the leash tightens
  (monitoring → enforcers → the hunt). Declared on purpose. **Chip-fragments are not economy** (mystery spine).

**The stat set (LOCKED — every stat gates real content; nothing decorative):**
- **Money (credits)** — the one wallet. Gates gear / disguise / bribes / upgrades.
- **Charge** (the engine's `energy`, reskinned) — paces the day (costs on actions/travel), refilled at the
  cradle; a vulnerability once she's hunted.
- **Capabilities / upgrades = INVENTORY items** — each upgrade is a thing she owns and installs (a buyable
  loadout; content gates on *owns-it*). Not a meter.
- **Chip / memories = INVENTORY items** — recovered fragments are collectibles (recovering one fires its
  memory beat; a *memories* view holds them). Not a meter.
- **Per-target lock = relation + corruption** (the target's own built-in traits; exact use set per character
  at casting, Step 4):
  - **relation** = the **infiltration** — embedded under a cover, works for him, he trusts her (*"I'm in your
    world"*). Built by the work/trust grind.
  - **corruption** = the **seduction** — how far she's hooked / compromised him (*"I'm in your head and your
    bed"*). Built by the seduction grind; extends smoothly into Act 2 (*hooked → owned*). **Replaces npc
    arousal (removed).**
  - Both high → he beds her → the weapon (climax → control canvas → drain).
- **Deliberately NONE:** her arousal · a feeling/"humanity" meter · a heat/suspicion meter. The company's
  crackdown / the leash is handled by **story beats + flags**, not a tracked bar.

**Scope (LO):** building **Phase 1 only** for now — up to the chip / the fracture. Phase 1 ends on a
**cliffhanger** (the fracture into Act 2), *not* a frontier-plateau — correct for a slice toward the whole.

**PARKED (known open questions, not skipped — Act-2 design):** **pacing/frontier** (the kill-or-love peak +
the livable post-game plateau + the endless-sandbox signpost). Phase-1 pacing is already carried by the web

## The opening (design) — the on-rails cage, then the first free step

> The agreed opening sequence. **Mostly on-rails** (Continue → Continue) across three beats — the cage —
> until one hinge node where the city opens. **~23 nodes** before she reaches Renner. Its job: show her as the
> most owned thing in the building, introduce the cast through *action* (never a lore dump), and hide three
> cracks the player sees and she doesn't. Everything she believes about herself is the lie the game takes apart.
> *(Beat = a chunk of story; node = one screen the player clicks. One beat → many nodes. Supersedes the early
> "bed → cradle" opening sketch.)*

**Shape:** Beat 1 (office) → Beat 2 (night) → Beat 3 (morning) → *out the door* → the Anchor / Renner.
**The hinge:** the final morning node — *out the door* — flips the game from on-rails to open (the city map +
real choices switch on). The twenty-odd Continue screens before it are the point: the first free step has to
*feel* like something after being owned.

### Beat 1 — The office (~12 nodes) — the punishment + the setup
1. **The line-up** — she and the three units stand before Mercer; the failed op hangs in the air.
2. **The accusation** — they had the rogue, she froze, he's gone. *(introduces the rogue + her freeze)*
3. **The threat** — he threatens to scrap her; the units stand blank. *(flavor choice: beg / silent / explain — same outcome)*
4. **She begs** — her surrender on display; she pleads to keep serving.
5. **The verdict** — too valuable to destroy ("the Chairman's investment" — *names the Chairman + her worth*); punishment instead.
6. **The punishment, set up** — he'll use her, here, now, in front of them.
7–9. **The punishment (~3 nodes, flexes ±)** — he takes her → the act (explicit, her body answering) → the units watching, blank, while *she* feels it. *(the "she feels, they don't" mirror)*
10. **Gratitude** — she thanks him; the degradation she accepts.
11. **The reassignment** — names Vega / Lyra / Nova to the head-on hunt; gives *her* the inside job ("useless with a gun, but…"); frames the mission: *the rogue murdered the Chairman's wife, enemy of the company and the world.*
12. **Dismissed** — out of the office → the night.
- **Introduces:** Mercer (cruel owner) · the three units (perfect, empty — her opposite) · the Chairman (named, the power above) · the rogue / mission (the "monster") · her (the owned asset who failed).
- **Hidden crack:** the freeze = the **first glitch.** Everyone reads it as a malfunction.

### Beat 2 — The night (~7 nodes) — the cradle, fully linear
1. **The walk back** — through the Tower to her own floor and room.
2. **The cradle** — she powers into the charging cradle; the reset ritual. *(the cradle = charge / save / start-of-day)*
3. **The tears** — her body cries; she can't explain the water; reads it as a fault to hide.
4. **The leak** — a memory fragment surfaces (a face, a sound, a name she doesn't know), then gone.
5. **The catechism** — she recites what she's told she is: *saved by the company and the Chairman, owes them everything, exists to obey.*
6. **The power** — her gift (control of a man the instant he finishes inside her, company-given) — and the odd fact it's **never** worked on the boss, never questioned.
7. **Power-down** — she promises to do better; powers down. *(the retreat into the leash)*
- **Introduces:** who she *thinks* she is (the lie). **Plants:** the awakening (tears + memory) + the boss-immunity mystery.
- **(No flavor choices — kept fully on-rails by design.)**

### Beat 3 — The morning (~4 nodes) — the task, then the city opens
1. **Power-up** — she wakes in the cradle, charged, a new day. *(the day-cycle / morning start)*
2. **The briefing** — a dossier waiting on her phone. *(the phone)*
3. **The tip** — what happened (a facility burned), why her (Renner knows the trail), what she can do (get close, the gift), where (the Anchor).
4. **Out the door** *(the hinge)* — she takes a cover and steps out of the Tower for the first time → **the city opens.** → the Anchor / meet Renner.

1	# The four lanes — when to use each, and how to write them
2	
3	NPC content uses four mechanisms. They are the SAME canvas+trigger engine; the
4	"lane" is the *combination of trigger fields* (the per-lane fingerprints below — `references/engine-reference.md`
5	has the full field reference). An NPC arc is built **across** lanes, sized by the NPC's arc shape (budget
6	table below). Read this before authoring any `npc_intro` / `arc_escalation` / `cross_npc` / `capstone` beat.
7	
8	**Two companion references:** pick each NPC's gating *spine* — which trait drives the arc, by shape —
9	per `references/trait-design.md` (don't gate every NPC on `relation`). The repeatable explicit layer
10	(after the first-night capstone) is the **sex-loop menu**, its own pattern — `references/sex-loop.md`.
11	
12	## The lanes at a glance
13	| Lane | Who picks | Player POV | Intent |
14	|---|---|---|---|
15	| **1 — Hub button** | Player clicks a menu item | "I'll click Tease." | Intentional escalation; high agency |
16	| **2 — Location-entry random** | Dice on room entry | "I walked in and he was…" | Ambient coexistence; texture |
17	| **3 — Dispatcher substitution** | Dice inside a Maya-solo activity | "I was showering and he walked in." | Charged surprise; happens *to* her |
18	| **4 — Capstone** | Engine, on threshold cross | "The night he caught me." | One-shot milestone; point of no return |
19	
20	## The master rule — Lane 1 leads
21	> Lane 1 leads the arc; Lanes 2/3 follow as consequences of Lane 1 escalation; Lane 4 capstones
22	> gate the milestones, fired by the stat/flag combos Lane 1 produces.
23	
24	The player clicks Lane 1 → stats rise → at thresholds, Lane 2/3 content *lights up* and Lane 4
25	capstones fire. "The world fills out around me as I escalate." So: **every arc is enterable from a
26	cold start** (corruption 0, no flags) through ordinary presence — the Lane 1 hub's base renders
27	unconditionally (presence floor). Never gate an arc's entry on a stat only raisable *inside* that
28	arc — that's the **"backwards on-ramp"**: the door locked behind a key that lives on the far side of
29	it, so the arc can never be entered from a cold start.
30	
31	## The 3×3 grid — mix lanes AND tiers
32	Within each lane, intensity scales with stat tier. A game that is all-one-lane feels wrong:
33	all Lane 1 = transactional "menu game"; all Lane 2 = inert/passive; all Lane 3 = no agency.
34	**Mix all three lanes across all three tiers → alive.** Lane 4 sits outside the grid (the milestones).
35	
36	## Per-arc-shape budget — the canvas-distribution matrix
37	Each arc shape (chosen per `references/trait-design.md`) has a per-lane canvas budget — L1 escalation
38	rungs / L2 ambients / L3 walk-ins / capstones, plus a per-shape total. **These are FULL-game targets
39	and the matrix below is the single source of truth** — size every arc against it; cell values are
40	guidelines, not quotas (the NPC's design brief commits to a specific number within each range).
41	
42	| Lane / Tier | Family/ambient | Slow-burn family | Peer/dating | Service | Antagonist/witness |
43	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
44	| **L1 / T1** | 1–2 base + 1–2 self-display | 1 (room visit) | 1 (visit at workplace) | 1 (workplace base) | 0–1 (shared-space neutral) |
45	| **L1 / T2** | 1–2 mid escalation | 0–1 (charged moment) | 0–1 (date intro) | 0 | 0 (no escalation register) |
46	| **L1 / T3** | 1–2 explicit | 0–1 (consummation if vocab allows) | 0–1 (commit beat) | 0 | 0 |
47	| **L2 / T1** | 1–2 morning/passing | 0–1 (corridor) | 1 (workplace ambient) | 1 (workplace texture) | 1–2 (presence beats) |
48	| **L2 / T2** | 2–3 evening/charged | 0–1 (charged corridor) | 0–1 (low density) | 0–1 | 1–2 (charged presence) |
49	| **L2 / T3** | 1–2 late-night/explicit | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0–1 (confrontation precursors) |
50	| **L3 / T1–T3** | 4–7 walk-ins on chores | 1–3 (discrete revelation walk-ins) | 0 | 0 | 0 own (appears in others' L3) |
51	| **Capstones** | 4–6 (catch, declare, first-night, sleepover, confrontation) | 3–5 (transitions + revelation + relationship turn) | 3–4 (dating chain) | 1–2 (hire + escalation if vocab allows) | 1–2 (confrontation, resolution) |
52	
53	**Total canvas budget by shape:**
54	
55	| Shape | Total | Notes |
56	|---|---|---|
57	| **Family/ambient** | **25–35** | The dense shape; the gold standard. Lane 3 is the dominant lane (~47%). |
58	| **Slow-burn family** | **10–15** | Sparse but focused; each revelation beat is concentrated, not a routine. |
59	| **Peer/dating** | **8–12** | Quest-chain progression; capstones do the heavy lifting. No Lane 3. |
60	| **Service** | **6–10** | Bounded by workplace register. No Lane 2 or 3. |
61	| **Antagonist/witness** | **6–10 standalone** | + cross-appearances in others' arcs. Standalone count is low; presence saturates the family arcs' lanes. |
62	
63	How the skill applies that budget:
64	
65	- **Empty cells are honest.** Peer/dating → no Lane 3. Service → no Lane 2 or 3. If the shape has 0 in
66	  a cell, the brief commits to 0 — filling an empty cell with relational/atmospheric texture to "fill out
67	  the world" is the failure, not the omission. (This governs the L2/L3 *escalation* surfaces; it never
68	  excuses a missing presence hub — see the next note.)
69	- **L1 cells count escalation *rungs*, not hubs.** The number of Lane 1 **hubs** is set separately by
70	  presence: **one Lane 1 hub per distinct `[[npcs.schedules]]` row** (location × window). An NPC
71	  scheduled across 5 windows has 5 hubs even with a tiny rung budget — the extra hubs are *light*
72	  (base + talk + leave), exposure-tier-capped, not extra escalation. Even a service/antagonist NPC gets
73	  a light hub at each scheduled location. Presence floor (a hub) and escalation register (the rungs on
74	  it) are independent axes.
75	- **Offscreen schedule rows are exempt from the hub rule.** A row at an `offscreen = true` location
76	  (the NPC's home/sleep/away block) is a non-navigable label — the player can't go there, so it gets
77	  NO hub and is exempt from the presence floor (`references/location-design.md`, the Day System). Use
78	  offscreen rows to complete an NPC's day without manufacturing dead presence. Only **reachable** rows
79	  earn a hub; **locked** rows follow the unlock contract (the locked-location unlock contract in
80	  `references/location-design.md`).
81	- **A third independent axis the L3 cells don't count: the player's own daily loop.** The L3 cells count
82	  *NPC walk-ins*, correctly shape-gated (a peer doesn't barge into private chores). They do NOT count the
83	  player's solo daily activities — sleep, eat, bathe, self-care feeders, the earning chore — which exist

85	  daily routine and a feeder floor. Misreading "0 walk-ins" as "no daily loop" is how games ship dead
86	  kitchens and solo-forever baths.

88	  distribution onto a peer/dating shape produces Lane 2/3 surfaces where neither belongs.
89	- **Budgets are always full-game.** Author each arc to its full per-shape budget — every game is the

91	  target, not a fraction of it.

96	Where the player both interacts with an NPC AND does solo work at one location, that's THREE

155	   `is_repeatable = true`, `location`, `schedules`. The parent activity (work a shift, shower,

187	     the player is standing.
188	   - **Cross-room siblings (peep / occupied / caught):** "is he in the *other* room" ships via the
189	     `npc_at_location` occupancy predicate — the peep, occupied-bathroom, and caught family, the
190	     cross-room counterpart of the co-location walk-in. Author them ONLY at a **user-confirmed** shared
191	     private space (`run-mode.md` Mode A; `content-framework.md` §5H). The compact model:
192	     - **The occupied room stays ENTERABLE; occupancy gates the ACTIVITIES, not the door.** A hard
193	       `entry_conditions` lock turns "occupied" into a dead-end (the engine renders only the
194	       `blocked_message` + a Go-back link — no activities), so the peek can't live there. For a shared
195	       private room you want interactive while occupied (a bathroom): keep it enterable; make the
196	       **description dynamic** (name the occupant when there is one); and gate each activity by occupancy
197	       on its own `conditions` — the player's **shower/self-care** shows only when the room is empty
198	       (`is_absent`); the **peek** shows only when the NPC is in there (`is_present`), and it lives **ON
199	       the bathroom canvas**, not a hallway. Reserve a hard `entry_conditions` lock for **genuinely
200	       SEALED** rooms (a locked office you earn a key to) where the dead-end IS the intent.
201	     - **The peek** — a solo-link on the bathroom canvas, gated on the NPC present, `max_triggers_per_day = 1`:
202	       ```toml
203	       [[canvases]]
204	       id = "peek_npc_shower"
205	       [canvases.trigger]
206	       location             = "loc_bathroom"
207	       is_repeatable        = true
208	       max_triggers_per_day = 1
209	       conditions = { version = "1.0", items = [
210	         { type = "npc_at_location", npc_id = "npc_X", location_id = "loc_bathroom", operator = "is_present" },
211	       ] }
212	       ```
213	       Base beat ≈ **30 flat words** (the image carries it); the player's read is **one `thought_bubble`**,
214	       not woven into the paragraph. For several housemates, the engine shows whichever one is actually in
215	       there (each peek gates on its own NPC). Escalate by stat tier — only the **deepest, once-per-arc
216	       tier** earns a dialog line + capstone density.
217	     - **Caught (an NPC catches the showering player) — catch-then-react.** Don't make the player
218	       pre-choose to "leave the door open." The shower is one terse activity; getting caught is
219	       **automatic by chance**, authored as a `substitution_only` target on the shower's trigger (rolls on
220	       entry), gated on a `chance` + the NPC's arc + **who's home now** (gate on the NPC's current
221	       location being a residence room — their schedule puts them home — **never a fixed time-of-day
222	       window**, so morning catches the morning-home housemates and evening the evening ones for free).
223	       It routes to a **short interstitial** that gives the agency *as a reaction*: a corruption-gated
224	       **flash/show vs cover-up/shut-it** choice. Only the bold branch routes into the longer capstone
225	       payoff. `max_triggers_per_day = 1` is the re-fire guard.
226	     - **Overhear** = the same occupancy gate, authored audio-only (no image).
227	
228	     Engine: the `npc_at_location` condition type lives in `setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied`
229	     (`v2.py:3711`) — operator `is_present`/`is_absent`, optional `npc_id` (omitted = the room itself
230	     occupied/empty). It evaluates in canvas, choice, substitution, AND `entry_conditions` (one canonical
231	     evaluator). The condition block needs `version = "1.0"` or it fails OPEN. Register stays RTS-flat
232	     (~30w base, scheme in a `thought_bubble`); the capstone it routes into is where density is earned.
233	     *(Note: two-NPC co-presence — "catch two of them together" — needs a separate engine feature the
234	     renderer doesn't have yet; only the player-is-a-party configs above are buildable today.)*
235	   - **Rising frequency (the saturation curve):** a single substitution rule's `chance` is a fixed
236	     constant, so one rule = a flat hijack rate forever — the tell of a routine that never escalates. To
237	     make the hijack **climb** (early = never; late = most visits), **stack several Pattern A rules on the
238	     same host**, one per corruption band, with **disjoint `gte`/`lt` conditions** so exactly one band is
239	     eligible at a time, and a **`chance` that rises per band**:
240	     ```toml
241	     # on the solo-activity host's [canvases.trigger]
242	     substitutions = [
243	       { target_canvas_id = "scene_npc_walks_in", chance = 0.10,
244	         conditions = { version = "1.0", items = [
245	           { type = "trait", subject = "player", trait_key = "corruption", operator = "gte", value = 10 },
246	           { type = "trait", subject = "player", trait_key = "corruption", operator = "lt",  value = 25 } ] } },
247	       { target_canvas_id = "scene_npc_walks_in", chance = 0.35,
248	         conditions = { version = "1.0", items = [
249	           { type = "trait", subject = "player", trait_key = "corruption", operator = "gte", value = 25 },
250	           { type = "trait", subject = "player", trait_key = "corruption", operator = "lt",  value = 45 } ] } },
251	       { target_canvas_id = "scene_npc_walks_in", chance = 0.70,
252	         conditions = { version = "1.0", items = [
253	           { type = "trait", subject = "player", trait_key = "corruption", operator = "gte", value = 45 } ] } },
254	     ]
255	     ```
256	     Each band item is the engine's typed `trait` condition (`subject = "player"`, `trait_key`,
257	     `operator`, `value` — verified `v2.py:3508`; `gte`/`lt` are real operators, `v2.py:3420`). Because
258	     the bands are disjoint, only the matching band's rule passes `_tryRule`, and each Pattern A rule rolls
259	     its OWN `Math.random() < chance` (`v2.py:4946`) — so the felt frequency steps up band by band. (Each
260	     `conditions` block needs `version = "1.0"` or it fails OPEN. This is the Pattern A path, NOT
261	     `exclusive_group` — these rules don't share a dice roll; they're gated apart by band so only one is
262	     ever live. To gate on the corruption *tier* 0–5 instead of the raw 0–100 odometer, use
263	     `type = "corruption_level"` — `v2.py:3700` — but for a saturation curve the raw-trait bands above are
264	     what you want.)
265	- **Vocabulary:** he walks in (mid-activity), he arrives while she's vulnerable, innocent setup →
266	  charged shift. The setup is genuinely a chore; the seduction happens *to* her.
267	- **A solo activity is also the game's earning/utility loop** — "work a shift" earns money and is the
268	  natural Lane 3 host. Splitting work (host) from the NPC hub (Lane 1) is the "three surfaces are
269	  separate canvases" rule above in action.
270	- **Self-care chores are first-class hosts too — not just "work a shift."** Shower, bath, sleep, eat are
271	  the highest-volume routine surface; at a location an NPC shares, each carries a dispatcher by default.
272	  A self-care canvas authored as a bare restore (no solo-lewd
273	  branch, no substitution) where an NPC is present is the **dead-bath anti-pattern** — it throws away the
274	  game's biggest content channel.
275	- **A solo host can fire a PLAYER-LEWD event, not only an NPC walk-in** (the player thread —
276	  `references/content-framework.md` §2; designed at `step-4-deep-design.md` Pass 1, structured at
277	  `step-5-blueprint.md` Pass 1).
278	  The walk-in (the dispatcher `if`) and the feeder (the solo `else`) are the **same canvas, not two
279	  systems** — the *fused unit*. The solo branch is the **player/world lewd
280	  track** — solo self-acts, location flashing/exhibitionism, public dares, job-lewd — the *base activity
281	  itself being lewd*, gated on the **player** `corruption`/`exhibitionism` tier and raising those odometers
282	  every time, hit or miss. This is the **corruption-feeder economy**: the supply that makes NPC seduction
283	  floors (the player-corruption gates on NPC seduction rungs) reachable. *Which* feeders exist and what each is
284	  worth is designed in the **player thread** (Step 4 story → Step 5 blueprint, `content-framework.md` §2E
285	  count); they then live **on the host canvas** as its solo branch. A game with rich NPC arcs but no feeder
286	  floor on its daily loop starves its player odometer (the Last Call finding).
287	
288	## Lane 4 — capstone (how to write)
289	**Fingerprint:** `priority ≥ 9` (typically 9–12), `trigger_mode = "manual"`, auto-fire on location
290	entry when conditions match, flag-gated + sets a one-shot flag on completion. **Repeat field is one of
291	two forms:**
292	- `is_repeatable = false` — once it fires, done; OR
293	- `is_repeatable = true` **+ a self-gate on its own setter flag** — the "retry" variant. The
294	  self-gate is a normal typed trigger condition on its OWN completion flag, e.g.
295	  `{ type = "flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "<its_setter_flag>", operator = "is_false" }`
296	  ("flag_is_false" is doctrine shorthand — emit the typed condition, NOT a literal `flag_is_false`
297	  key, which the engine ignores). The canvas re-fires next eligible time *until* its flag is set, so
298	  a **Refuse branch that doesn't set the flag keeps it alive** (the branching-fork retry rule below).
299	  Use this whenever a branching capstone has a decline path.
300	
301	Three types: **A** linear deterministic, **B** branching choice (both branches playable, diverge in
302	downstream effect), **C** quest-chain step. **Type-B forks follow the branching-fork rules:** both
303	branches written good-faith (no "obviously wrong" decline), the choice diverges in *downstream* effect
304	not on-the-spot reward, the fork sits at the **terminal** beat (don't branch mid-scene then re-converge),
305	a refuse path is retryable (doesn't burn the flag — the retry variant above), and the fork doesn't
306	compound (one decision per capstone, not a tree). Per-NPC capstone budget per shape (table above). Voice:
307	Tier-3 earned (once-only, so the prose can spend).
308	
309	**Gate a capstone on the ODOMETER, never the throttle** (`references/trait-design.md` "Throttle vs
310	odometer"). A capstone is a one-shot permanent milestone, so it gates on a **permanent** axis —
311	`player.corruption` (the depravity odometer) and/or `npc.relation`/`npc.corruption` — **plus its flag
312	chain**. NEVER gate it on `arousal`: that's a **throttle** (resets at climax), which belongs on the
313	**repeatable** sex-loop content, not a one-shot. Pick the odometer by who-initiates: NPC-initiated
314	dating → `npc.relation`; NPC-initiated seduction → player `corruption` + the relationship flags (the
315	NPC's `arousal` throttle then drives the repeatable loop afterward, and colors the hub prose
316	heat-framed). The split-spine failure to avoid is about an **odometer**: a relation/own-corruption
317	meter the hub builds that the milestone never reads (LC's Marcus — relation gates only capstone #1).
318	
319	**The repeatable layer comes after.** Capstones are the once-only *first* time; the replayable
320	explicit surface that follows (opened from the hub once the first-night flag is set) is the
321	**sex-loop menu** — its own pattern, see `references/sex-loop.md`.
322	
323	## Voice register
324	- **Lane 1 / 2 / 3:** RTS-flat default — ~30-word caption density, direct/crude diction per the NPC's
325	  **per-tier vocab ceiling** (declared in its design brief; the ceiling model is
326	  `references/kink-ceilings.md`, default-to-maximum-explicit). Re-readable (these repeat).
327	- **Lane 4 capstones:** Tier-3 EARNED — interior monologue + layered sensory detail +
328	  character-distinguishing diction. Once-only, so the prose can spend.
329	- **Choice labels** are tighter than the prose — label = action, no subtext, crude-in-label at the
330	  ceiling, emoji on menu buttons / bare on in-loop beats (Lane 1 above + `references/sex-loop.md`).
331	- **Mode, not just density.** The flat register governs how *dense* the prose is, not whether people
332	  speak. Where a beat is an actual exchange — player ↔ NPC, or a group in one room — carry it in `dialog`
333	  blocks (their words, interruptions, refusals), not a narrated summary of what was said; RTS plays
334	  dialogue even in its explicit scenes (the full mode-not-density rule is `references/rts-flat-prose.md`).
335	  **Lean hardest at the hot beats** (capstones, sex, confrontations): narrating the encounter as summary
336	  is the worst drift — play them. Multi-party beats give each present NPC a voiced moment under the
337	  no-monologue cap (one terse beat each, not a speech). EXEMPT only when **no one's there to speak**:
338	  solo activities, voyeur/peek where you're unseen, and the interior-monologue stretches of a capstone.
339	  A present NPC is not exempt — even a mood glimpse gives them one terse line.
340	
341	## Runtime rendering rules (live-verified — these bite even when the build is green)
342	The location screen renders four separate paths; a canvas only appears if it matches the right one:
343	- **An NPC hub needs `npc` set, not just `requires_npc` — separate fields.** `requires_npc` gates
344	  presence only; `npc` sets the `npcId` that `renderNpcPortraits` requires
345	  (`selectNpcPortraitCanvasesForLocation` skips `!c.npcId`, `v2.py:4065`). A repeatable hub with
346	  `requires_npc` but no `npc` renders as a flat **solo link**, not a portrait. Lane 2 ambients likewise
347	  need `trigger_mode = "random"` + `chance` or they render as links instead of rolling on entry. Set
348	  both on hubs; random+chance on ambients. (Full engine trace + grep guard: `toml-gotchas.md`.)
349	- **NPC first-contact one-shot → make it AUTO-FIRE**, NOT an NPC-portrait canvas. `renderNpcPortraits`
350	  skips non-repeatable canvases, so a one-shot *with* `npc`/`requires_npc` set renders NOWHERE (it's
351	  neither a repeatable portrait nor an auto-fire). Author it like the boot canvas: `is_repeatable=false`,
352	  `priority≥9`, **no `npc`/`requires_npc`**, gated on flags; it auto-fires on entry and sets the
353	  `<npc>_opened_up` flag. The ongoing **hub** (repeatable, `npc` set) renders the portrait from then on.
354	- **Solo activity → no per-canvas `schedule`** if it should be available whenever the location is
355	  reachable. A `schedule` block on a solo activity suppressed its button (match the proven
356	  `activity_make_tea` shape: location + `is_repeatable` + `priority` + optional `conditions`/`substitutions`,
357	  no `schedule`). Gate availability via `conditions` and location reachability instead.
358	- **Distinct `name` per canvas.** A non-repeatable first-contact and its repeatable hub sharing a
359	  `name` collide in the name-group selector — give them different `name`s.
360	- **A hub portrait renders only while the NPC is present** (`getNpcLocation(slug).location == here`).
361	  If a hub won't show, verify the NPC's `[[npcs.schedules]]` actually places them at that location at
362	  the current time (and that schedule slugs resolved). Presence is the gate, not just `is_active`.
363	- **Presence-on-nav is FREE — surface it.** The nav cards already paint avatars of the NPCs scheduled at
364	  each *destination* (`getNpcsPresentAtLocation`), so the player can see *who's there* before spending
365	  time to travel — the same schedule source the hub + the occupancy door read (see
366	  `references/location-design.md` on presence-on-nav).
367	  You get this just by authoring schedules + hubs where the NPCs actually are; it's a reason to anchor a
368	  hub at the NPC's real location, not a convenient one. (Pairs with travel-friction: see who's home, then
369	  decide if the trip is worth the hour.)
370	
371	## Beat type → lanes (what a beat authors)
372	- `npc_intro` → establish the NPC's **Lane 1 hub(s)** (one per schedule row) + optionally the first **Lane 2** ambient. Cold-start enterable.
373	- `arc_escalation` → add **Lane 1 rungs** (locked-visible) AND the **Lane 2/3** content that lights up at those thresholds — per the shape's budget, respecting empty cells.
374	- `economic` → usually a **solo work activity** (Lane 3 host that earns money) + its dispatcher; keep it OUT of any NPC hub (the work-is-a-separate-canvas rule).
375	- `cross_npc` → an NPC as interruptor in another's **Lane 3** ending, or a shared scene.
376	- `capstone` → a **Lane 4** one-shot gating a milestone.
377	- `location_reveal` / `story_turn` → structure + the scenes the new place/turn needs (often a hub + ambients).
378
